action.name: Multiattack (hunter)
action.text: Gerhard makes three attacks: one with its hooves and two with its maul. It can replace a maul attack with a hooves attack.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d8 + 8) piercing damage.

action.name: Hooves
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (2d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Maul
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (4d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Charge (beast)
action.text: Gerhard moves up to 20 feet in a straight line without provoking opportunity attacks, and can pass through the spaces of Large or smaller creatures. If it moves through a creature's space during that movement, the target must make a DC 22 Dexterity saving throw, taking 19 (2d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage and being knocked prone on a failed save. If Gerhard ends this movement in a creature's space, the creature is pushed out to the nearest unoccupied space.

action.name: Spectral Slaughter (hunter; Recharge 5-6)
action.text: Gerhard sends forth up to six spectral duplicates of itself to strike down enemies within 120 feet of itself. Each enemy can be targeted by no more than two duplicates. Each duplicate makes a maul attack against a target that deals 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage on a hit. 	Gerhard can then use a bonus action to move up to 120 feet in a straight line towards one of the targets without provoking opportunity attacks and make a maul attack.

action.name: Stance (Bonus Action)
action.text: Gerhard changes between stances, either standing on all fours (beast) or standing on its hind legs (hunter), granting it certain features noted by that stance name. Dash (Beast). Gerhard moves up to 40 feet.

reaction.name: Dodge (beast)
reaction.text: If Gerhard's speed isn't 0, and it is targeted by a melee attack, it moves back 10 feet without triggering opportunity attacks. If this causes Gerhard to leave the attack's reach, it evades the attack completely, causing it to miss.

reaction.name: Retributive Strike (hunter)
reaction.text: After taking damage, Gerhard makes one maul or hooves attack.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (2/Turn)
legendary.text: Gerhard can take 2 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. Gerhard regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Focus (hunter; 1/Day)
legendary.text: Gerhard regains 21 (6d6) hit points and recharges its Spectral Slaughter.

legendary.name: Maul
legendary.text: Gerhard makes one maul attack.

legendary.name: Regenerate
legendary.text: Gerhard regains 21 (6d6) hit points.

legendary.name: Howl (beast)
legendary.text: Gerhard releases a monstrous howl. Each creature of Gerhard's choice within 60 feet of it that can hear it gains 14 (4d6) temporary hit points.

fields.description:
There once lived a noble and valiant paladin named Gerhard. A guardian of the people and a symbol of hope, he fought tirelessly to protect the city from the countless dangers that threatened its existence. Revered by the townsfolk, he stood as a bastion of light amid the encroaching darkness.
	However, fate had other plans for Gerhard. On one of his many quests, he stumbled upon a cursed artifact of great and terrible power. In his bravado, he unleashed the curse upon himself, and the darkness within the artifact began to seep into his very being. His once-pure soul was tainted, and his body began to twist and warp into a monstrous, unrecognizable form.
	As Gerhard's transformation grew more pronounced, he realized that the curse was beyond his control. Unable to bear the thought of harming the people he had sworn to protect, he made the ultimate sacrifice.
	Gerhard implored his companions to banish him, to bind him in chains and cast him into an unfathomable abyss from whence he could never escape. In a final act of love for the city he had served so faithfully, Gerhard surrendered himself to a fate worse than death.
	His comrades, their hearts heavy with sorrow, reluctantly agreed to carry out his wish. They bound the tortured knight in enchanted chains, forged with the power to contain even the most potent of dark forces. With a solemn oath to honor his memory and uphold his legacy, they consigned Gerhard to the depths of the abyss, where his monstrous form would be forever hidden from the world.
	And so, Gerhard's tragic tale came to an end —or so it seemed. Deep within the abyss, Gerhard has now entirely succumbed to the curse. His mind, once sharp and filled with purpose, has been obliterated, leaving behind only the instincts of a ravenous beast. The remnants of his once-noble spirit are lost, devoured by the darkness that has consumed him entirely. His selfless act saved the city of Luyarnha from the devastation he might have unleashed, but at a terrible cost to himself.
	The reason his comrades chose banishment over granting him the release of death was the fear that the curse would spread upon his demise. They believed that if Gerhard were to die, the dark power would be unleashed, seeking new hosts to corrupt and destroy. Thus, they condemned their friend to an eternity of suffering, bearing the weight of the curse alone, to ensure the safety of Luyarnha and the world beyond. And so, the tale of Gerhard, the once-proud knight, now a monstrous beast in the depths of the abyss, remains a somber legend, talked about only among those who still remember his name.

None shall slay him, and he shall only know suffering.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 393 (Indie)

fields.name: The King of the Hunt
fields.languages: all but rarely speeks, telepathy 120 ft.
fields.immune: poison, radiant; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks

trait.name: Fey Ancestry
trait.text: The King has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put the King to sleep.

trait.name: Great Cleave (3/Day)
trait.text: When the King makes a melee weapon attack, it can make another attack with the same weapon against each other creature within reach and within 5 feet of the original target as part of the same action.

trait.name: Leap Attack
trait.text: Once per turn, if the King moves at least 15 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a greatsword attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 6 (1d12) slashing damage.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (5/Day)
trait.text: If the King fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: The King has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Reactive
trait.text: The King can take one reaction on every turn in combat.

trait.name: Special Equipment
trait.text: The King has an Unbound Épée Solaire (SGttEH page 256). The king can't be disarmed of it while it is conscious. The bonus to attack and damage rolls is already included in the stat block.

trait.name: Undying Warrior
trait.text: Having 0 hit points doesn't knock the King unconscious. He must still make death saving throws, and suffers the normal effects of taking damage while at 0 hit points.

trait.name: Unstoppable
trait.text: The King's speed can't be reduced, but effects like being paralyzed can still prevent it from moving.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The King makes three greatsword attacks, or four shortswords attacks if the Unbound Épée Solaire is transformed.

action.name: Greatsword
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 32 (6d6 + 11) slashing damage and 4 (1d8) radiant damage. If the King damages a creature twice on a turn with this attack, the target must succeed on a DC 25 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of the King for 1 minute. A frightened creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

action.name: Shortsword
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (3d6 + 11) slashing damage and 4 (1d8) radiant damage.

action.name: Hunter's Pursuit (Bonus Action)
action.text: The King flies up to 70 feet toward a creature it can see without provoking opportunity attacks.

action.name: Misty Step (Bonus Action)
action.text: The King casts misty step. Charisma is its spellcasting ability for the spell.

action.name: Vicious Finisher (2/Day) (Bonus Action)
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +16 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 138 (20d12 + 8) slashing damage. This attack scores a critical hit on a result of 15-20 on the die. The King can use this bonus action twice, once each when the King has fewer than half, and one-quarter its hit points.

reaction.name: Dodge Step
reaction.text: When a creature the King can see attacks it, the King can move 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks and make a Dexterity saving throw with a DC equal to the attack roll's total. On a success, the King evades completely and the attack misses. On a failure, the King takes half the attack's damage if it hits it.

reaction.name: Killing Blow
reaction.text: If the King sees a creature within its reach fall to 0 hit points, it can make an attack with its weapon against the creature. On a hit, the King pierces a vital organ and the target immediately dies.

reaction.name: Weapon Parry
reaction.text: The King adds 8 to its AC against one attack that would hit it. To do so, the King must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon. If the attack is a ranged attack, the King can beckon gravity and force the attacker to make a DC 26 Strength saving throw, pulling it up to 60 feet straight towards the King on a failure. This reaction can't be used two turns in a row.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (3/Turn)
legendary.text: The King can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The King regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Enforced Duel
legendary.text: The King magically teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. Before teleporting, it can force a creature that it can see within 120 feet of it to make a DC 26 Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the target is teleported to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the King's destination.

legendary.name: Strike
legendary.text: The King makes a greatsword attack or two shortsword attacks, depending on which form its weapon is in.

legendary.name: Mark of the Hunt (costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text: The King marks its prey for death. Each creature of its choice in a 300 feet of it that it can see must succeed on a DC 26 Charisma saving throw or be branded for 1 minute. The King gain a +7 bonus to damage rolls against branded targets. Any attack roll the King makes against a branded target is a critical hit on a roll of 18-20 on the d20. If a branded target dies, the King regains 30 hit points. The brand can be removed via a remove curse spell or similar effect.

fields.description: Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 396 (Indie)

fields.name: Gwena
fields.immune: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered

trait.name: Keen Hearing and Smell
trait.text: The scourge lycan has advantage on Perception checks that rely on hearing or smell.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The scourge lycan makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its claws.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.

action.name: Claws
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage.

action.name: Devour (recharge 4-6)
action.text: The scourge lycan attempts to eat a creature within 5 feet of it. The target must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the creature is crunched by the werewolf, taking 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage and falling prone. The scourge lycan regains hit points equal to the damage dealt.

fields.description:
As the scorching moon rises, beasts become restless, cobbles crack, and the air sizzles with savage suspense. Fiery claws cauterise as they rend, and Luyarnha is choked with the scent of charred flesh.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 404 (Indie)

fields.name: Kaspar

trait.name: Flexible Combatant
trait.text:
When the hunter draws or stows a weapon, it can draw or stow another weapon with the other hand. It can reload weapons with the loading, reload, or barrel properties without a free hand.
	Additionally, if the hunter is carrying a one-handed melee weapon in one hand, and a one-handed ranged weapon in the other hand, it doesn't have disadvantage on attack rolls with ranged weapons from being within 5 feet of a hostile creature.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The hunter makes two longsword attacks. If it has a firearm drawn, it can also make a firearm attack.

action.name: Longsword
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) slashing damage if used with two hands.

action.name: Firearm
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 60/120 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

reaction.name: Dodge Step (3/short Rest)
reaction.text: If the hunter's speed isn't 0, and it is targeted by an attack, it dodges in defense. It moves 5 feet, and makes a Dexterity saving throw with a DC equal to the attacker's attack roll's total. On a success, it evades completely and the attack misses. On a failure, it halves the attack's damage against itself if the attack hits. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.

fields.description:
Kaspar is a former hunter of the Radiant Order who retired when he got older and slower. He hung up his sword and now works as a painter. Beneath a gruff exterior, Kaspar is kind-hearted, but he has become suspicious and withdrawn due to past traumas. His milky white hair and sun-darkened skin testify to his years in the field. He's willing to help the party defend themselves if they prove they're willing to stand up against the horde.

Hunter:
The motto of hunters is "survive together, or die together." They never hunt alone, unless they are forced to. After all, even the oft considered greatest hunter, Steinhardt, was always accompanied by Vicar Priscilla on all his hunts. The nights in Luyarnha can be brutal and the beasts relentless, and only a united front can hope to survive.
	All jaegers are hunters, but not all hunters are jaegers. Where jaegers are relentless killers, hunters are often simple citizens wishing to protect their homes and those they love. They are often the first to perish, but fear the one who lives long in a profession where men die young. Hunters are an invaluable contribution to the survival of the city-state and its denizens, and successful hunters cut down hundreds of beasts throughout their life before succumbing to the fires of battle.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 404 (Indie)

fields.name: Father Hauke

trait.name: Spellcasting
trait.text:
The zealot is a 5th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). The zealot has the following cleric spells prepared:

	• Cantrips (at will): light, sacred flame, thaumaturgy
	• 1st level (4 slots): cure wounds, guiding bolt, silvered shell
	• 2nd level (3 slots): lesser restoration, spiritual weapon
	• 3rd level (2 slots): mass healing word, protection from energy

trait.name: Call to Radiance
trait.text: As a bonus action, the zealot can expend a spell slot to magically imbue its weapons with divine power. Until the end of the turn, its melee weapon attacks deal an extra 10 (3d6) radiant damage on a hit. If the zealot expends a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the extra damage increases by 1d6 for each level above 1st.

action.name: Mace
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage.

fields.description:
Father Hauke is a middle-aged man with a tall and thin build. He has a gaunt face and deep-set eyes that betray his weariness. He is dressed in the traditional robes of his faith, adorned with intricate golden embroidery. Father Hauke speaks with a strong and confident voice, but his eyes reveal a hint of doubt and uncertainty. He is a priest of the Radiant Church and a man of faith who has recently grown doubtful in the face of how bad Geistnacht has turned out. As much as he wants to believe all will be well, he can't help but feel the night is only worsening. Despite his doubts, he is determined to do the right thing and protect his congregation.

Zealot:
Zealots are fanatical followers of the Radiant Church. The Church believes that the Radiant One holds the key to free Luyarnha of its scourge, just as he brought them enlightenment. As such, these zealots do their utmost to spread their message and gather converts. They know that actions speak far louder than words and as such are always at the forefront of each hunt. They are trained in the art of combat, but they prefer to use their abilities to heal and support their allies, strengthening the faith of their comrades through their unwavering devotion. They are often willing to make the ultimate sacrifice in the name of their deity, if it means saving their kin.
	Despite their peaceful demeanor, zealots are capable of incredible violence, driven by their faith to defend the Radiant Church and its followers. Although their doctrine is one of tolerance, direct insults to their god are deemed heretical and they will not hesitate to use their powers to quiet the offender. They are often seen leading Radiant Church expeditions, accompanied by a retinue of hunters, as they seek to bring the light back to Luyarnha after its fall from grace.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 409 (Indie)

fields.name: Maddon Gillet
fields.skill: Deception +5, Insight +4, Investigation +5, Perception +6, Persuasion +5, Sleight of Hand +4, Stealth +4

trait.name: Cunning Action
trait.text: On each of its turns, the spy can use a bonus action to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

trait.name: Sneak Attack (1/Turn)
trait.text: The spy deals an extra 7 (2d6) damage when it hits a target with a weapon attack and has advantage on the attack roll, or when the target is within 5 feet of an ally of the spy that isn't incapacitated and the spy doesn't have disadvantage on the attack roll.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The spy makes two melee attacks.

action.name: Shortsword
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Hand Crossbow
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

fields.description:
Maddon is a pale-skinned young orc with slicked-back dark brown hair and a crooked smile that he often uses to show off his gold-capped canine tooth. The rogue has worked for Lord Thomathin Rehwoldt for many years as a go-between for the noble and the city's more criminal elements. While his dark clothing helps him blend in with the shadows, his vanity and wealth are on full display in the form of gold trinkets that he often casually flashes.
	The shady orc has a policy of always looking out for himself first, but the current situation in the city has him concerned. To protect his business interests, he provides assistance to the characters wherever and whenever possible.

Spy:
Rulers, nobles, merchants, guildmasters, and other wealthy individuals use spies to gain the upper hand in a world of cutthroat politics. A spy is trained to secretly gather information. Loyal spies would rather die than divulge information that could compromise them or their employers.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 415 (Indie),
		Monster Manual (2014) p. 349

fields.name: Lord Rehwoldt

action.name: Rapier
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.

reaction.name: Parry
reaction.text: The noble adds 2 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the noble must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

fields.description:
Lord Thomathin Rehwoldt is a narcissist that values reputation and power above all else. It does not matter to him how the plague affects the city, only that the church has blamed him. It's apparent that Thomathin is not necessarily a good person, but he is true to his word and keeps his promises to friends and rivals. He is honestly unaware of the research the sect was conducting and is eager to accuse the Radiant Church simply out of retaliation for implicating him. Thomathin doesn't care who is blamed for the plague, that the beasts are infected citizens, or if the church is even truly guilty; repairing his reputation and power are all that matter to him.

Noble:
Nobles wield great authority and influence as members of the upper class, possessing wealth and connections that can make them as powerful as monarchs and generals. A noble often travels in the company of guards, as well as servants who are commoners.
	The noble's statistics can also be used to represent courtiers who aren't of noble birth.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 418 (Indie),
		Monster Manual (2014) p. 348

fields.name: Borast Deepreaver

trait.name: Encircling Strikes
trait.text: Encircling Strikes. Once per turn, when the jaeger attacks from the opposite side of a creature from where it started its turn, or attacks while on the opposite side of a creature from an ally, it deals an additional 3 (1d6) damage on a hit.

trait.name: Evasion
trait.text: If the jaeger is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, the jaeger instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

trait.name: Flexible Combatant
trait.text:
When the jaeger draws or stows a weapon, it can draw or stow another weapon with the other hand. It can reload weapons with the loading, reload, or barrel properties without a free hand.
 	Additionally, if the jaeger is carrying a one-handed melee weapon in one hand, and a one-handed ranged weapon in the other hand, it doesn't have disadvantage on attack rolls with ranged weapons from being within 5 feet of a hostile creature.

trait.name: Hemorrhaging Wound (recharge 5-6)
trait.text:
The jaeger can't use this trait on the first round of combat. When the jaeger hits a creature with a blade attack, it rends a vicious wound. At the end of each of the target's turns, it loses 17 (5d6) hit points. Each time the target takes damage from this effect, the number of dice of damage it takes at the end of its next turn is reduced by one, and the bleeding stops when the number of dice is reduced to 0. A bleeding creature can make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, after taking the damage, ending the effect on a success. The DC equals 15 + half the number of dice of damage remaining (rounded down).
	If the jaeger hits a bleeding target with a blade attack, the target doesn't gain a new wound, but its wound's damage resets to 5d6.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
trait.text: The jaeger's weapon attacks are magical.

trait.name: Piercing Gaze (1/Day)
trait.text: The jaeger gains darkvision out to 120 feet and the effect of see invisibility for 1 hour (no action required).

trait.name: Sharp Senses
trait.text: Whenever the jaeger uses its Dodge Step, Weapon Parry, or Chasing Finisher, it gains advantage on its next attack roll.

trait.name: Special Equipment
trait.text: The jaeger wields a dream executioner. Alternatively it can be wielding an orphan's cradle, a serpent bladewhip, or a meat hookshot. Its blade attack and references to it are replaced with an attack made with the respective weapon.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The jaeger makes three blade attacks. If it is wielding a firearm, it can also make one firearm attack.

action.name: Blade
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) slashing damage.

action.name: Firearm
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, range 60/120 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage.

action.name: Chasing Finisher (recharge 5-6)
action.text: The jaeger moves 40 feet and makes a blade attack. On a hit, the target takes an additional 14 (4d6) slashing damage.

reaction.name: Dodge Step (3/short Rest)
reaction.text: When a creature the jaeger can see attacks it, if its speed isn't 0, it moves up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks and makes a Dexterity saving throw with a DC equal to the attack roll's result. On a success, it evades completely and the attack misses. On a failure, it takes only half damage if the attack hits.

reaction.name: Weapon Parry (3/short Rest)
reaction.text: The jaeger fires off a bullet to deflect an attack that it can see within 60 feet of it. To do so, the jaeger must be wielding a firearm. It reduces the attack's damage by 13 (1d10 + 8). If this reduces the damage to 0, the attacker is stunned until the start of its next turn, as the bullet hits a nervous junction.

fields.description:
Borast is an experienced monster hunter who specializes in eldritch creatures and supernatural events. He has leathery nutmeg skin, and his jet-black beard and hair are braided with silver wire. A creature's claw left three scars across his right cheek and eye. The gruff and suspicious dwarf prefers to work alone and is unhappy that Lord Rehwoldt hired the characters. However, he begrudgingly admits that his currently incapacitated state precludes him from completing the mission and helps the party in whatever way he can.

Jaeger:
The jaegers of Luyarnha stand as the city's premier line of defense, a formidable force whose might singlehandedly turned the tides of battle in the First War. These warriors exhibit an unwavering commitment to their city, always the first to answer the call of duty and often the last thing their adversaries see. In their hands, the jaegers wield potent trick weapons gifted to them by the Church and other factions dedicated to the city's salvation. With these instruments of destruction, they can decimate entire squadrons of beasts and humanoids, nimbly evading attacks and relentlessly pursuing their quarries until their blades sink into their targets.
	The mysterious process of their creation is closely guarded by their creators, the enigmatic Obitus Scholare. With the ongoing city lockdown, however, the ranks of the jaegers have been gradually thinning. They fall in battle more rapidly than new jaegers can be forged. It is the hope of all citizens that Luyarnha can stem the tide of the Scourge before their mightiest shield shatters.
	Every jaeger's life revolves around a strict regimen of training and battle, honing their skills and reflexes beyond the potential of mere mortals: with each kill, they sharpen their instincts, bolstering their own strength and becoming harder to kill-an unfortunate truth that applies even to those of them who lose their sanity. Jaegers are the city's greatest hope and the embodiment of its deepest fear-the jaegers, ever the hunters, ever the hunted.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 419 (Indie)

fields.description:
Vicar Henri Inonder is outwardly a good and righteous man who works tirelessly to give succor to the poor and needy. His perfect smile, warm brown eyes, and perfectly groomed appearance hide a bottomless pit of greed and corruption. Henri is a member of the Obitus Scholare, the secret sect that was harvesting the eldritch being's remains. His twin brother, Vargas Inonder, was transformed into the augmented assassin that devolved into madness. After the sect's destruction and himself being injured, Henri now works to conceal the truth behind accusations aimed at the aristocracy and Lord Thomathin in particular because of an old grudge between them. He feverishly works to find a cure before succumbing to the madness like his brother.
	The Vicar is a master manipulator who is proficient in Deception and Persuasion. He hides his festering injury and resulting beast-like transformation behind an alter self spell while working to find a cure for himself. A successful DC 25 Arcana check or detect magic spell indicates the Vicar is using magic to alter his appearance. If dispelled, it reveals that he is almost entirely mutated into one of the bestial creatures.

Priest:
Priests bring the teachings of their gods to the common folk. They are the spiritual leaders of temples and shrines and often hold positions of influence in their communities. Evil priests might work openly under a tyrant, or they might be the leaders of religious sects hidden in the shadows of good society, overseeing depraved rites. A priest typically has one or more acolytes to help with religious ceremonies and other sacred duties.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 421 (Indie),
		Monster Manual (2014) p. 348

fields.name: Vargas the Scorched

trait.name: Guiding Light
trait.text: The adjudicator sheds dim light in a 10-foot radius. When a creature starts its turn in the light, or enters it for the first time on a turn, it gains disadvantage on Charisma saving throws until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Limited Telepathy
trait.text: The adjudicator can magically communicate ideas, emotions, and images telepathically with any creature within 120 feet of it. This form of telepathy doesn't allow the receiving creature to telepathically respond.

trait.name: Reactive
trait.text: The adjudicator can take one reaction on every turn in combat.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The adjudicator makes two handaxe attacks.

action.name: Handaxe
action.text: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage. On a hit, if the adjudicator isn't within 5 feet of the target, the adjudicator can teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target.

action.name: Soul Tear
action.text:
Soul Tear. Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (4d8 + 3) necrotic damage and the target must succeed on a DC 14 Charisma saving throw or its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken.
	This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a long rest. If this effect reduces a creature's hit point maximum to 0, the creature dies. A creature killed by this reduction can't be resurrected until the adjudicator is killed.

action.name: Inferno (recharge 4-6)
action.text: Flames pour down from the adjudicator's wings. Each creature between 10 and 40 feet of the adjudicator must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

reaction.name: Snuff Out the Light
reaction.text: When a spell that restores hit points is being cast within 120 feet of the adjudicator, the adjudicator teleports to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the caster and makes a handaxe attack against it with advantage. On a hit, the spell fails and has no effect.

legendary.name: Lair Actions
legendary.text:
On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), Vargas takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects; Vargas can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

	• Vargas siphons shadowy energy from the crucified elder being, increasing his power and mending his wounds. He regains 4d10 hit points, and until the start of the next round, his weapon attacks deal an additional 1d10 necrotic damage.

	• Vargas wields the maddening energy of eldritch blood and sends a wave of madness at any creature he chooses within sight. Each creature must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or gain a short-term madness effect (see "Steinhardt's Madness System,"
page 269).

	• Vargas calls out for aid, and two fallen luyarnhians drop down from above, aiding him in the fight.

fields.description:
Failed Experiments:
In their lust for power, the Obitus Scholare lead gruesome experiments, merging the flesh of soldiers with that of eldritch beings. Their labor gave birth to powerful combatants, and a sea of corpses. Scorched adjudicators are the fruits of such experiments, humanoids that couldn't become true warriors, failing to resist the call from beyond and losing their sanity. Yet, the scholars still found a use for these failures: they now act as perfect killers for their creators.

Enforcers of Justice:
Adjudicators enforce justice, more specifically, the brand of justice approved of by the Obitus Scholare. Indeed, these abominations are dispatched to remove any threat to the order, their otherworldly powers trapping the souls of their victims and ensuring an irreversible death. The murderous intent of these monsters is apparent in battle; they delight in causing suffering and their deadly instincts prevents healing. Deriving a twisted sense of pleasure from their hunts, adjudicators often carry the shrunken, decapitated heads of their victims as horrific mementos.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 425 (Indie)

fields.name: Lord Jasper Roth

action.name: Rapier
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.

reaction.name: Parry
reaction.text: The noble adds 2 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the noble must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

fields.description:
Lord Jasper Roth is a successful nobleman from a minor house in Luyarnha. He is widely known for his philanthropic efforts and support of the Radiant Church, particularly in medicinal treatments. Lord Jasper hires the party to find alchemist Klaus von Brunheimer, who lives in Jägerweiler, a nearby village that has recently gone silent. In particular, he was funding Klaus's research into various tonics and remedies that might help alleviate the current pandemic sweeping the city. Since the nobleman paid for Klaus' research and he is no longer in contact, Lord Jasper wants the party to retrieve it for him. He stresses the need for professional discretion, offering a generous sum of 1,500 gp up front, and promises 3,000 gp when the party returns with the research.

Noble:
Nobles wield great authority and influence as members of the upper class, possessing wealth and connections that can make them as powerful as monarchs and generals. A noble often travels in the company of guards, as well as servants who are commoners.
	The noble's statistics can also be used to represent courtiers who aren't of noble birth.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 430 (Indie),
		Monster Manual (2014) p. 348

fields.name: Bram LeGrand The Acolyte

trait.name: Divine Eminence
trait.text: As a bonus action, the priest can expend a spell slot to cause its melee weapon attacks to magically deal an extra 10 (3d6) radiant damage to a target on a hit. This benefit lasts until the end of the turn. If the priest expends a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the extra damage increases by 1d6 for each level above 1st.

trait.name: Spellcasting
trait.text:
The priest is a 5th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). The priest has the following cleric spells prepared:

	• Cantrips (at will): light, sacred flame, thaumaturgy
	• 1st level (4 slots): cure wounds, guiding bolt, sanctuary
	• 2nd level (3 slots): lesser restoration, spiritual weapon
	• 3rd level (2 slots): dispel magic, spirit guardians

action.name: Mace
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage.

fields.description:
Bram LeGrand is a quiet young man in his early twenties with a slight stammer and a nervous tick in his left eye. He spends most of his days cloistered with research books and studying the teachings of the Radiant Church. His aunt, Lieutenant Captain Adelle Roux of the city watch, stepped in after his mother (Adelle's sister) passed away years ago and has been looking out for him ever since. He respects his aunt, but feels smothered at times.
	Bram stays out of harm's way as much as possible in combat, assisting where he can. As an observer and trainee, he has limited capabilities and often makes poor decisions that put his life in danger.

Priest:
Priests bring the teachings of their gods to the common folk. They are the spiritual leaders of temples and shrines and often hold positions of influence in their communities. Evil priests might work openly under a tyrant, or they might be the leaders of religious sects hidden in the shadows of good society, overseeing depraved rites. A priest typically has one or more acolytes to help with religious ceremonies and other sacred duties.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 432 (Indie),

	• Cantrips (at will): fire bolt, light, mage hand, prestidigitation

	• 3rd level (3 slots): counterspell, fireball, fly

action.name: Dagger
action.text: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

action.text: Any spellcaster that can cast the find familiar spell (such as an archmage or mage) is likely to have a familiar. The familiar can be one of the creatures described in the spell (see the Player's Handbook) or some other Tiny monster, such as a crawling claw, imp, pseudodragon, or quasit.

fields.description:
Cerwyn Raolet is an older man in his late sixties with tight leather skin covered in liver spots. His body has been mutated and twisted into unnatural angles from exposure to the eldritch powers mingling with his blood. A bitter and curmudgeonly person who prefers the company of books over people, Cerwyn was a recluse who specialized in combining alchemy with the arcane. The Obitus Scholare sought him out for this expertise, and used him to flood Jägerweiler with alchemical acid to kill their failed experiments and witnesses. Afterward, they attempted to kill the angry mage, but he managed to escape. He's now hiding in these ruins and plotting revenge against those who tricked and wronged him. The mad mage lacks empathy towards life and sees what he did to Jägerweiler Village as nothing more than experimentation in the name of progress. He has no qualms about murder if it furthers his research.

Mage:
Mages spend their lives in the study and practice of magic. Good-aligned mages offer counsel to nobles and others in power, while evil mages dwell in isolated sites to perform unspeakable experiments without interference.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 439 (Indie),
		Monster Manual (2014) p. 347

fields.description:
Percival (LN human mage) is an arcane scientist and has been with the Scions for three years. He is an expert in the magical and alchemical arts, focusing on studying arcane constructs. He IS an accomplished inventor, instrumental in the advancements made on the blue-flame custodians. He is often seen experimenting with new spells and enchantments, as well as researching ancient texts in search of lost knowledge. While his research has yielded some impressive results, he rarely reveals his findings to the public, preferring to stay anonymous. He is not pleased to be here in the temple and only came because the custodians were disappearing.

	Personality Trait. "I'm always tinkering with something new, even if I don't know what it is yet."

	Ideal. "Knowledge is power, and I strive to uncover secrets that others have overlooked."

	Bond. "I am devoted to my research and the Scions, and will do whatever it takes to help them succeed."

	Flaw. "My curiosity often gets the better of me, leading me to take risks that may be too great."

	Quote. "It's not enough to know something; you must understand it."

Mage:
Mages spend their lives in the study and practice of magic. Good-aligned mages offer counsel to nobles and others in power, while evil mages dwell in isolated sites to perform unspeakable experiments without interference.

fields.name: Lost Ones

trait.name: Eldritch Resilience
trait.text: The swarm has advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects.

trait.name: Litany's Influence
trait.text: At the start of each of the swarm's turns, each character within 60 feet of it must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the character takes psychic damage equal to the swarm's hit points divided by 20, rounded down, (e.g., 50 psychic damage at 1000 hit points) and cannot take reactions until the start of their next turn. On a success, they take half as much damage and are unaffected by the reaction restriction.

trait.name: Swarm Movement
trait.text: The swarm moves as a single entity, occupying a 25-foot by 25-foot space. For every 200 hit points the horde loses, each side of its area shrinks by 5 feet.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The swarm makes four Melee attacks.

action.name: Melee
action.text: Use a single attack roll with an attack bonus equal to the swarm's hit points divided by 70, rounded down (e.g., +14 at 1000 hit points), range: 15 ft., one target. Hit: (10d6) bludgeoning damage. This damage is reduced by 1d6 for each 100 hit points the swarm has lost.

action.name: Overwhelm
action.text: If the swarm has more than half of its hit points remaining, it can use its action to attempt to overwhelm a character. The target must make a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the swarm's Strength (Athletics) check, with a bonus equal to the swarm's hit points divided by 50, rounded down (e.g., +20 at 1000 hit points). On a failure, the target is grappled (escape DC 20).

fields.description: Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 472 (Indie)

fields.name: Aspect of Glutony

trait.name: Blood Frenzy
trait.text: The gluttony has advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its hit points.

trait.name: Shapechanger
trait.text: The gluttony can use its action to polymorph in the last thing that it fed upon of Huge size or smaller, or back into its true form. Its statistics, other than its size and special move, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: When the gluttony assumes the form of a creature it has devoured, it becomes indistinguishable from a normal specimen of that creature's species. Only a spell such as trueseeing or similar spell of 6th level or higher can reveal the Gluttony's true form.

trait.name: Unwieldy
trait.text: Other creatures must use 15 feet of speed to try to move the Gluttony 5 feet.

action.name: Ravenous Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) piercing damage. The gluttony regains hit points equal to half the damage dealt. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or be cursed with an insatiable hunger. Each curse bestows a level of exhaustion, and multiple curses accumulate. The exhaustion persists until the cursed creature consumes food during a short or long rest, is targeted by a remove curse spell, or consumes a goodberry. Regardless of how many curses have accumulated, fulfilling any of these conditions removes all hunger curses at once.

action.name: Devour
action.text: Gluttony can devour an unconscious or dead creature of Medium or smaller size. If the creature was alive it immediately dies. The gluttony gains resistance against all damage until the start of its next turn and 9 (1d10 + 4) temporary hit points.

fields.description:
Madwalker 1st Level

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 160 (Indie)

fields.name: Aspect of Envy

trait.name: Amphibious
trait.text: The envy can breathe both air and water

trait.name: Magic Envy (Recharge 6)
trait.text: If a 1st or 2nd level spell is cast within the Envy's line of sight, it can immediately use its reaction to cast the same spell, without requiring any components, against a valid target of envy's choice.

trait.name: Pack Tactics
trait.text: The envy has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the envy's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The envy makes two attacks, either two bites or two Eye of Envy attacks.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Eye of Envy
action.text: Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) psychic damage, and until the start of the envy's next turn, whenever the target regains hit points, the envy regains the same amount.

fields.description:
Madwalker 3rd Level

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 160 (Indie)

fields.name: Aspect of Disgust

trait.name: Acid Skin
trait.text: A creature that touches the disgust or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 3 (1d6) acid damage. Each hit on the disgust with a nonmagical weapon made of metal or wood induces corrosion. After dealing damage, the weapon suffers a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to damage rolls. The weapon is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. Nonmagical ammunition made of metal or wood that hits the disgust is destroyed after dealing damage.

trait.name: Stench
trait.text: Any creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of the disgust must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the start of its next turn. On a success, the creature becomes immune to the disgust's stench for the next 24 hours.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The disgust makes three Gastric Spit attacks.

action.name: Gastric Spit
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 2) acid damage.

action.name: Disgusting Vomit (Recharge 5-6)
action.text: The disgust expels acid in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 13 (3d8) acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. After this initial effect, all creatures within 20 feet of the disgust (whether they were in the cone or not) must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the end of their next turn due to the nauseating sight. On a successful save, the creature is immune to the disgust's Disgusting Vomit for 24 hours.

fields.description:
Madwalker 5th Level

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 161 (Indie)

fields.name: Aspect of Sloth

trait.name: Surge of Action (Recharge 5-6)
trait.text: As a bonus action, the sloth can move up to its speed toward a hostile creature that it can see.

trait.name: Aura of Laziness
trait.text: Creatures that start their turn within 15 feet of the sloth have their speed halved for that turn. If the creature ends its turn inside the aura, it must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom saving throw or become restrained until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Regeneration
trait.text: The sloth regains 5 hit points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hit point.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage. The target must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 3 (1d6) poison damage, can't take reactions until the end of its next turn, and has its speed halved until the end of the sloth's next turn. On a successful one, the target takes half as much damage and doesn't suffer the other effects.

action.name: Claw
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

fields.description:
Madwalker 7th Level

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 161 (Indie)

fields.name: Aspect of Pain

trait.name: Thorns
trait.text: The pain is covered in thorns. A creature that touches the pain or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet takes 4 (1d8) piercing damage.

trait.name: Suffering
trait.text: Damage dealt by the pain ignores temporary hit points and resistances. If pain reduces a creature to 0 hp while it has temporary hit points, it falls unconscious and is dying as normal.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The pain makes three attacks with its Painful Claws.

action.name: Painful Claws
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) slashing damage and the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have disadvantage on its next attack roll or ability check due to intense pain.

action.name: Excruciating Pain
action.text: The pain targets one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target creature must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target creature takes 13 (3d6 + 3) psychic damage, falls prone, and drops any held equipment.

action.name: Thorn Rain (recharge 5-6)
action.text: The pain launches a volley of thorns in a 20-foot radius around it. Each creature in that area must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 18 (4d8) piercing damage and becoming impaled with thorns on a failed save, or half as much damage and no impalement on a successful one. A creature impaled with thorns takes an extra 7 (2d6) psychic damage each time it takes damage until it completes a long rest or is targeted by a lesser restoration spell or greater. A creature can only be affected by one thorn impalement at a time.

fields.description:
Madwalker 9th Level

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 162 (Indie)

fields.name: Aspect of Lust

trait.name: Shapechanger
trait.text: The lust can use its action to polymorph into a Small or Medium humanoid, or back into its true form. Its statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

trait.name: Charm Opportunist
trait.text: Attacks made by lust that hit a charmed creature are automatically considered critical hits.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: Lust makes three melee attacks.

action.name: Creepy Slam
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) psychic damage.

action.name: Tentacle
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage, and if the target is Large or smaller, it is grappled (escape DC 16). Until this grapple ends, the creature is restrained, and lust can't attack another target with a tentacle.

action.name: Mind Overload
action.text: The lust targets one charmed creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 14 Charisma saving throw, taking 5d10 psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. This attack doesn't end the charmed condition on a creature.

action.name: Spellcasting
action.text:
The lust casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 18, +10 to hit with spell attacks).

	• At will: command
	• 3/day each: charm person, hold person
	• 1/day each: charm monster, dominate beast, hypnotic pattern

action.name: Fascinating Presence
action.text: Each creature of lust's choice that is within 60 feet of it and aware of it must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or become charmed for 1 minute or until lust or its allies harm the target. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

fields.spells: Command, Charm Person, Hold Person, Charm Monster, Dominate Beast, Hypnotic Pattern
fields.description:
Madwalker 11th Level

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 162 (Indie)

fields.name: Aspect of Sadness

trait.name: Dispel Master
trait.text: The sadness can cast dispel magic as a bonus action and it is always considered as if it was cast using a 5th level spell slot.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: The sadness has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Melancholy Magic
trait.text: When a creature fails a saving throw against a spell cast by the sadness, it has disadvantage on all saving throws until it finishes a short or long rest.

trait.name: Sad But True
trait.text: When the sadness dies, it explodes in a burst of psychic energy. Each creature within 15 feet of it must make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw, taking 13 (3d8) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The sadness makes two Creepy Slam attacks.

action.name: Creepy Slam
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) psychic damage.

action.name: Planar Shift (2/Day)
action.text: The sadness can cast plane shift (self only) twice per day to shift from the Material Plane to the Penumbral Plane, or vice versa.

action.name: Spellcasting
action.text:
The sadness casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16, +8 to hit with spell attacks):

	• At will: detect magic, dispel magic, fire bolt, shocking grasp
	• 3/day each: faerie fire, identify, counterspell, detect thoughts, fireball, misty step
	• 1/day each: banishment, cloud kill, globe of invulnerability, stoneskin, wall of force

fields.spells: Detect Magic, Dispel Magic, Fire Bolt, Shocking Grasp, Faerie Fire, Identify, Counterspell, Detect Thoughts, Fireball, Misty Step, Banishment, Cloud Kill, Globe of Invulnerability, Stoneskin, Wall of Force
fields.description:
Madwalker 13th Level

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 163 (Indie)

fields.name: Aspect of Pride

trait.name: Prideful Grappler
trait.text: The pride has advantage on attack rolls against creatures it is grappling.

trait.name: Armor of Pride
trait.text: Whenever an enemy attack misses the pride it gains a cumulative +1 to AC until the start of its next turn (up to +5).

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The pride makes three Claws or three Force Blast attacks. If the pride hits at least one attack with its Claws, it can make a Grab with its remaining attacks against the target hit.

action.name: Force Blast
action.text: Ranged Spell Attack: +9 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (1d10 + 6) force damage.

action.name: Claws
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 5) slashing damage.

action.name: Grab
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: the target is grappled (escape DC 17). Targets that are Huge or larger are immune.

action.name: Spellcasting

fields.description:
Madwalker 15th Level

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 163 (Indie)

fields.name: Aspect of Greed

trait.name: Covetous Globes
trait.text: Greed watches over the material world from the Penumbral Plane via its magical Mask of Scrying. When they spy an appropriate target, usually some crusading do-gooder or powerful noble, they shift to the Material Plane and attack with their covetous globes. The globes cause enough damage to seem like a real threat, but this is a ruse. Their real power lies in the transmission of the Curse of Greed.

trait.name: Curse of Greed
trait.text: Every day at dusk, in which a victim of this terrible curse fails to accumulate at least 500 gp in gold, goods, or treasures, their maximum hit points are reduced by 2 (1d4) points. The curse cannot be lifted by a simple remove curse spell, but it does grant the recipient the knowledge of how to end the curse. To remove a Curse of Greed, the victim must permanently sacrifice at least 10,000 gold pieces in valuable items, such as useful magic items, family heirlooms of great sentimental value, or other treasures.

trait.name: Mask of Scrying
trait.text: Greed wears enchanted, bird like masks of bone covered in magical runes over their grotesque faces. The masks allow them to peer into the Material Plane at will, as if using the scrying spell, even if they are not currently on that plane. The mask crumbles to dust if removed from the emogun's person or if it dies.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The greed makes two attacks with its Claws and two with its Covetous Globes.

action.name: Claws
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.

action.name: Draining Touch
action.text: Melee Spell Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) necrotic damage, and the greed regains hit points equal to half the damage dealt.

action.name: Covetous Globes
action.text: Ranged Spell Attack: +9 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) necrotic damage. Each creature struck by a globe must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 17) or be afflicted by the Curse of Greed.

action.name: Planar Shift
action.text: The greed can cast plane shift (self only) to enter the Material Plane, cause mischief or attack with its covetous globes, then return to the penumbra to savor its victim's fate.

fields.description:
Madwalker 17th Level

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 164 (Indie)

fields.name: Aspect of Fear

trait.name: Guided by Fear
trait.text: The fear has advantage on attack rolls against creatures that are frightened.

trait.name: Shapechanger
trait.text: The fear can use its action to polymorph into a Small, Medium, or Large humanoid, or back into its true form. Its statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

trait.name: Terror Aura
trait.text: At the start of each of its turns, the fear gains 1d6 temporary hit points for each frightened creature within 30 feet of it.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The fear makes three Fear Stab or three Psychic Blast attacks.

action.name: Fear Stab
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) psychic damage. The target must succeed on a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

action.name: Psychic Blast
action.text: Ranged Spell Attack: +10 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 18 (2d10 + 7) psychic damage.

action.name: Spellcasting
action.text:
The fear casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 18, +10 to hit with spell attacks):

	• At will: darkness, detect magic, silent image
	• 3/day each: fear, major image
	• 1/day each: dream, phantasmal killer

action.name: Terror Wave (Recharge 5-6)
action.text: The fear emits psychic energy in a 40-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw, taking 27 (6d8) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failed save, the creature also becomes frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. On a success, the creature becomes immune to the fear's Terror Wave for the next 24 hours.

action.name: Planar Shift
action.text: The fear magically shifts from the Material Plane to the Penumbral Plane, or vice versa.

fields.spells: Darkness, Detect Magic, Silent Image, Fear, Major Image, Dream, Phantasmal Killer

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 165 (Indie)

fields.name: Arachne Serf

trait.name: Prowlers
trait.text: The creature has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide.

trait.name: Spider Climb
trait.text: The creature can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Web Sense
trait.text: While in contact with a web, the creature knows the exact location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

trait.name: Web Walker
trait.text: The creature ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The arachne serf makes two Claw attacks.

action.name: Claw
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.

action.name: Web Spinning
action.text:
The creature can spin webs to create difficult terrain or to restrain creatures. It can create webs to cover a 20-foot square for every 10 minutes of work. The terrain becomes difficult, and all creatures that touch the web must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or become restrained. The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed (each 20-foot square section has AC 10, hp 15, vulnerability to fire damage; immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage; if it takes fire damage, all linked web sections take the same damage on the following round and all creatures in the area take 1d6 fire damage).

Arachne Special Powers:
All Arachne monsters have this feature, but the madwalker cannot use it.

fields.name: Arachne Matriarch

trait.name: Prowlers
trait.text: The creature has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide.

trait.name: Spider Climb
trait.text: The creature can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Web Sense
trait.text: While in contact with a web, the creature knows the exact location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

trait.name: Web Walker
trait.text: The creature ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The arachne matriarch makes four Poisonous Claw attacks.

action.name: Poisonous Claw
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 6) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage. A hit creature must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 1 minute.

action.name: Poison Spray
action.text: The arachne matriarch sprays magic poison gas in a 40-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking 45 (10d8) poison damage and being poisoned on a failed save, or half as much damage and not getting poisoned on a successful one. At the end of each of its turns, a poisoned target can make a Constitution saving throw, ending the effect on a success.

action.name: Spellcasting
action.text:
The arachne matriarch casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks):

	• At will: charm person, mage hand, poison spray
	• 3/day each: dispel magic, sleep, fear, invisibility, see invisibility
	• 1/day each: dimensional door, dominate person, greater invisibility, mass suggestion, teleportation circle

action.name: Web (Recharge 5-6)
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one creature. Hit: The target is restrained by webbing. As an action, the restrained target can make a DC 15 Strength check, bursting the webbing on a success. The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed (AC 10; hp 10; vulnerability to fire damage; immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage).

action.name: Web Spinning
action.text:
The creature can spin webs to create difficult terrain or to restrain creatures. It can create webs to cover a 20-foot square for every 10 minutes of work. The terrain becomes difficult, and all creatures that touch the web must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or become restrained. The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed (each 20-foot square section has AC 10, hp 15, vulnerability to fire damage; immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage; if it takes fire damage, all linked web sections take the same damage on the following round and all creatures in the area take 1d6 fire damage).

Arachne Special Powers:
All Arachne monsters have this feature, but the madwalker cannot use it.

fields.name: Tanarean Pegasus

action.name: Hooves
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

fields.description:
The tanarean pegasus is a stunning creature, known for its striking beauty and natural grace. This breed of pegasus boasts an impressive wingspan of up to 20 feet, making it a highly coveted mount for those seeking swift transportation and superior strength. However, training and handling this creature can present unique challenges. The tanarean pegasus lacks the intelligence of its regular pegasus counterpart, making it skittish and difficult to gain trust and obedience from. These instincts of self-preservation and tendency to flee can make the training process longer and more complicated.

To train a tanarean pegasus successfully, a trainer must create a secure and comfortable environment, introduce it to other trained mounts to develop socialization skills, and establish trust through consistent, patient handling and training. Despite these challenges, the tanarean pegasus is a valuable asset in Tanares, with its beauty, strength, and speed making it a worthy mount for those willing to put in the effort to train it.

Cost to training and Flying Points:
Base: 6 Flying Points
Monthly Cost | Extra Flying Points
20 gp | +1d6
50 gp | +2d6
80 gp | +3d6
120 gp | +4d6

Flying Maneuvers:

Rescue (2 FP). You can save an ally from falling. Use your reaction to fly to an ally that is falling within your flying range and hold them in the air. Apply only if another flying mounted enemy caused the falling.

Dive (2 FP). Using your mount's flight superiority, you quickly get out of the way of danger. You can take a reaction when you succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against an effect from another flying mounted enemy that would cause you to take half damage, such as fireball, to take no damage from the effect.

Flight Tenacity (4 FP). You know the dangerous movements of mounted enemies that would make you fall from the griffon. Whenever you or your mount would begin to fall due to an effect caused by a flying-mounted enemy, you can use this maneuver as a reaction to prevent the fall, considering a failed saving throw or ability check, if any, as a success.

Aerial Sprint (2 FP). The pegasus' instinct takes over and it charges against the mounted creature. As a bonus action, the mount gains extra flying speed for the current turn. The increase equals twice its flying speed (after applying any modifiers), but the mount must move toward a target flying-mounted enemy.

Inspiring Flying (3 FP). All allies gain 2 Flying Points. The mount regains this use after finishing a short or long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 296 (Indie)

fields.name: Tanarean Griffon

trait.name: Keen Sight

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The griffon makes two attacks: one with its beak and one with its claws.

action.name: Beak
action.text: Beak: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage.

action.name: Claws
action.text: Claws: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage.

fields.description:
The tanarean griffon is a fearsome creature with the powerful body of a lion and the majestic wings and head of an eagle. With a more muscular body than a regular griffon, it is a formidable opponent in combat. Though the tanarean griffon lacks intelligence and magical abilities, it more than makes up for it with its ferocity and strength. This makes it a difficult creature to train and control, requiring a patient and skilled trainer to gain its trust and loyalty.

The tanarean griffon can be unpredictable and aggressive, with a tendency to assert dominance over weaker foes. To successfully train one, a trainer must establish their own dominance and earn the griffon's respect through consistent handling and training. Providing a secure and comfortable environment is crucial to developing the creature's trust and obedience. Despite its challenges, the tanarean griffon is a powerful and imposing creature that can serve as a mount or companion for those who are willing to put in the effort to train it.

Cost to training and Flying Points:
Base: 6 Flying Points
Monthly Cost | Extra Flying Points
25 gp | +1d6
60 gp | +2d6
90 gp | +3d6
130 gp | +4d6

Flying Maneuvers:

Flight Destabilization (3 FP). A powerful bull rush that can unbalance flying mounted enemies. As an attack, you try to destabilize the target's flight. The target must make a Dexterity or Strength saving throw with DC = 8 + griffon's Strength modifier + proficiency bonus. If it fails, it plummets towards the ground.

Winged Resilience (3 FP). The griffon's agility can be very effective against flying mounted enemies. Spend Flying Points to reduce the damage inflicted by a flying mounted enemy's attack by 12 points.

Flight Tenacity (4 FP). You know the dangerous movements of mounted enemies that would make you fall from the griffon. Whenever you or your mount would begin to fall due to an effect caused by a flying-mounted enemy, you can use this maneuver as a reaction to prevent the fall, considering a failed saving throw or ability check, if any, as a success.

Aerial Sprint (2 FP). The griffon' instinct takes over and it charges against a target flying mounted enemy. As a bonus action, the mount gains extra flying speed for the current turn. The increase equals twice its flying speed (after applying any modifiers), but the mount must move toward a target flying-mounted enemy.

Fearsome Claws (3FP). Three enemies lose 2 Flying Points. The mount regains this use after finishing a short or long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 297 (Indie)

trait.text: The hippogriff has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

trait.name: Flyby
trait.text: The hippogriff doesn't provoke opportunity attacks when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

action.text: The hippogriff makes two attacks: one with its beak and one with its claws.

action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) piercing damage.

action.name: Claws
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.

fields.description:
The tanarean hippogriff is a majestic creature with the body of a horse and the head and wings of an eagle. Like its regular hippogriff counterpart, it can grow up to 10 feet in length and possesses incredible speed and agility. However, the tanarean hippogriff lacks intelligence, making it challenging to train and control. It can be skittish and easily frightened, requiring a patient and skilled trainer to gain its trust and obedience.

To train a tanarean hippogriff successfully, a trainer must create a safe and comfortable environment and introduce the hippogriff to other trained mounts to develop socialization skills. The trainer must also establish trust through consistent handling and training. Despite its challenges, the tanarean hippogriff is a valuable and sought-after creature, prized for its speed, agility, and even beauty.

Cost to training and Flying Points:
Base: 4 Flying Points
Monthly cost | Extra Flying Points
15 gp +1d4
30 gp +2d4
50 gp +3d4
75 gp +4d4

Flying Maneuvers:

Flight Destabilization (3 FP). A powerful bull rush that can unbalance flying mounted enemies. As an attack, you try to destabilize the target's flight. The target must make a Dexterity or Strength saving throw with DC = 8 + hippogriff 's Strength modifier + proficiency bonus. If it fails, it plummets towards the ground.

Rescue (2 FP). Observing the movement of the mounted enemy, you can save your ally from the falling. Use your reaction to fly to an ally that falls within your flying range and hold them in the air. Apply only it another mounted creature caused the falling.

Winged Resilience (3 FP). The griffon's claws can be very effective against flying mounted enemies. Spend Flying Points to reduce the damage inflicted by a flying mounted enemy's attack by 12 points.

Forced Landing (1 FP). When a flying mounted enemy makes your mount fall, you can use this maneuver to land safely on the ground without suffering any damage from falling. Your mount can take to the air again on your next turn.

Inner Strength (3 FP). As a bonus action, you allow a creature to immediately use its reaction to make a maneuver using Flying Points, but with the cost reduced by 2. The mount regains this use after finishing a short or long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 298 (Indie)

fields.name: Tanarean Desert Drake
fields.speed: walk 30 ft., burrow 30 ft., fly 60 ft.

trait.name: Assault
trait.text: If the desert drake moves at least 15 feet before it hits with a Bite attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 4 (1d8) additional piercing damage.

trait.name: Wild Accuracy
trait.text: For each other desert drake within 30 feet, this drake receives +1 on attack rolls (max +5).

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage.

action.name: Necrotic Breath (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
action.text: The desert drake exhales necrotic energy in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must take a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

fields.description:
The drake is a formidable creature that strikes fear into the hearts of many adventurers. With its muscular body, sharp claws, and fiery breath, it is a formidable opponent in combat. The drake is a solitary beast that does not form bonds with others. This makes it difficult to train and control, as it will only obey those it is intimidated by. The drake is also intelligent and can be difficult to outsmart, requiring a trainer with considerable skill and experience. To gain dominance over a drake, a trainer must establish authority and maintain a constant level of intimidation. While firm vocalization and daunting body language are usually sufficient, drakes occasionally try to engage in fights to demonstrate physical superiority. Therefore, it will sometimes be necessary to resort to physical intimidation with them, but it must be administered carefully to avoid triggering a worse violent response. Once the drake has been subdued, it can be trained in a variety of techniques, such as hunting and aerial combat exercises.

Drakes are carnivorous creatures that feed on a variety of prey, such as mammals and other creatures of the sky. Their diet is essential to maintaining their physical strength and agility. Training a Drake is a dangerous and difficult task, but those who are able to successfully train one will have a loyal and powerful companion that will serve them well in any adventure.

Cost to training and Flying Points
Base: 8 Flying Points
Monthly cost | Extra Flying Points
50 gp | +1d8
120 gp | +2d8
250 gp | +3d8
500 gp | +4d8

Flying Maneuvers:
Winged Resilience (3 FP). The drake's tough scales are highly effective against mounted enemies in the air. Spend Flying Points to reduce the damage inflicted by a flying mounted enemy's attack by 12 points.

Flight Destabilization (3 FP). A powerful bull rush that can unbalance even the most skilled flying mounted enemies.

As an attack, you to try to destabilize the target's flight. The target must make a Dexterity or Strength saving throw with DC = 8 + drake's Strength modifier + proficiency bonus. If it fails, it plummets towards the ground.

Flight Blindness (4 FP). This powerful maneuver weakens the connection between a flying mount and its rider. It generates a powerful wave that interferes with their flight, preventing the mounted enemy from using any Flying Points until the start of your next turn. The only way to avoid this effect is to spend 6 Flying Points.

Forced Landing (1 FP). When a flying mounted enemy makes your mount fall, you can use this maneuver to land safely on the ground without suffering any damage from falling. Your mount can take to the air again on your next turn.

Final Breath (5 FP). The Drake's fiery breath is a fearsome weapon against flying mounted enemies. When you use it, you can also utilize any of your Flying Maneuvers at no cost against one of the targets the breath is aimed at. The drake this use after finishing a short or long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 299 (Indie),
		Tanares Sourcebook p. 306 (Indie)

action.text: The ridge drake exhales an icy blast in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw, taking 27 (5d10) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
