fields.description: Source:	Griffon's Saddlebag: Griffons of the Multiverse p. 42 (Indie)

fields.name: Lamplighter
fields.languages: understands Common but doesn't speak it

trait.name: Lantern Light
trait.text: The lamplighter emits a bright light with a radius of 20 feet and an additional 20 feet of dim light. If the lamplighter dies, the light goes out.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee attack roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 22 (4d8+4) Necrotic Damage.

action.name: Lantern Beams
action.text:
The Lamplighter fires two distinct magical beams from the lantern, targeting two visible objects within a 60 ft. radius.
Choose two from Blasting Light, Blinding Light, Burning Light or Witch Light.

action.name: Blasting Light
action.text: Strength saving throw: DC 13. Failure: 10 (3d6) force damage and the target is knocked prone. Success: Half damage only.

action.name: Blinding Light
action.text: Constitution saving throw: DC 13. Failure: 10 (3d6) radiant damage and the target is blinded. This condition lasts until the Lamplighter's next turn. Success: Half damage only.

action.name: Burning Light
action.text: Dexterity saving throw: DC 13. Failure: 10 (3d6) fire damage and the target has the Burning condition (3d6). Success: Half damage only.

action.name: Witch Light
action.text: Wisdom saving throw: DC 13. Failure: The target becomes charmed. While charmed, the target must spend all movement points to move towards the Lamplighter during their turn. The target makes a saving throw at the end of their turn, which, if successful, ends the effect. If the target takes damage from the Lamplighter, the saving throw used to end the effect is made with advantage. After 1 minute, the target is no longer charmed by the Lamplighter.

reaction.name: Warding Flare
reaction.text: Trigger: A creature targets the Lamplighter with an attack roll. Response: The Lamplighter flashes its lantern, and the target has disadvantage on attack rolls against the Lamplighter this turn.

fields.description:
The creature is draped in a dark, tattered, cloth covering its hunched back, from which hang two enormous lanterns. Its arms and legs are thin and long, making it walk on all fours as if on stilts. Its face is expressionless, pale, and its eyes like empty, black pools of water. When it opens its mouth, its jaws twist, revealing a gaping maw filled with sharp, hooked teeth. When the lanterns are lit, particles of arcane energy swirl around it, and the creature emits an agonizing shriek.

Combat Tactics:
During the day, the Lamplighters hide in dark, dilapidated buildings or huts, only appearing at dusk. They patrol the city all night, using magic to light up the destroyed streetlights, ensuring that the main roads are adequately illuminated.
	The soft glow emitted by the Lamplighters as they appear amidst the ruins can be seen from afar. These creatures use their "lantern beams" to repel other creatures from a distance or lure unsuspecting prey closer. Once the prey is close enough, the lamplighter attacks and devours them with its greedy maw.
	Lamplighters whose health drops to 1/4 or below typically flee to the ruins to recover. These creatures consider the streets where they worked when they were still human as their territory. Once healed, they return to their territory to continue protecting their precious lights from intruders.
	Since Lamplighters are naturally drawn to the dark areas of Drakkenheim, characters can usually avoid them by staying within areas already illuminated by their lanterns. Similarly, extinguishing the lights along the main roads will lure lamplighters to specific locations, forcing these creatures to relight their lanterns.

Study the enemy.
Characters with natural or survival skills gain Advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) checks when they Study a Lamplighter, learning the following based on the result:
(10+) You recognize the creature's resistances.
(15+) You know the creature's Lantern Beam ability and its multiple options.
(20+) You are aware of its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

Source:	In Search of Smuggler's Secrets p. 24 (Third Party)

fields.name: Alchemy Golem
fields.languages: understands the languages of its creator but can't speak
fields.resist: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks that aren't adamantine
fields.conditionImmune: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned

trait.name: Aversion to Fire
trait.text: If the alchemy golem takes fire damage, it has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Immutable Form
trait.text: The alchemy golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

trait.name: Lightning Absorption
trait.text: Whenever the alchemy golem is subjected to lightning damage, it takes no damage and instead regains a number of hit points equal to half the lightning damage dealt.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: The alchemy golem has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Monstrous Grafts
trait.text: The alchemy golem's weapon attacks, including monstrous grafts added by its creator, are magical. Monstrous grafts have a +6 attack bonus, deal twice the normal number of damage dice, and have a +5 bonus to their damage rolls. The alchemical golem can only have 1 graft in each slot.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The alchemy golem makes two melee weapon attacks.

action.name: Slam
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

fields.description: Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 43 (Indie)

fields.name: Death Snail

action.name: Leech
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) poison damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

fields.description:
A death snail is formed from a vile concoction of forest troll bone meal, giant eagle blood, and goblin bone meal, enclosed in a hollowed-out efreet horn, and sealed shut with an ettercap tongue. The resulting monstrosity possesses a dull intelligence, but its only impulse is to slay all creatures other than its master.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 364 (Indie),
		Complete Witch p. 19 (Indie)

fields.name: Flying Book
fields.conditionImmune: blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned

trait.name: Antimagic Susceptibility
trait.text: The flying book is incapacitated while in the area of an antimagic field. If targeted by dispel magic, the flying book must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against the caster's spell save DC or fall unconscious for 1 minute.

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: While the flying book remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal book.

action.name: Slam
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1 bludgeoning damage.

fields.description:
Little can be said about the flying book that is not readily apparent. Though it is indistinguishable from an arcanist's spellbook while motionless, this animated arcane tome can flutter through the air at a moment's notice, using its cover as rudimentary wings. Flying books are playful and enjoy the sensation of being written in.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 364 (Indie),
		Complete Witch p. 19 (Indie)

fields.name: Fright
fields.languages: understands all languages it knew in life but can't speak
fields.resist: acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, thunder, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks
fields.conditionImmune: charmed, exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
trait.text: The fright can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

action.name: Life Drain
action.text: Melee Spell Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 9 (2d8) necrotic damage. The target must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

fields.description:
Hauntings can often be attributed to the usual spectral suspects: ghosts, specters, shadows, and poltergeists. But benign hauntings, where a restless spirit merely plays tricks on the living, are usually caused by a fright. These spirits tend to be the artifacts of children or entertainers, clinging to the afterlife for company and a semblance of affection, and are as such preoccupied with fun. They never willingly harm others when they haunt a house, and they will serve any master that conjures them, if only for the sake of inclusion.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 365 (Indie),
		Complete Witch p. 20 (Indie)

fields.name: Grep
fields.languages: understands Common and Underdcommon but can't speak

trait.name: Ambusher
trait.text: The grep has advantage on attack rolls against any creature it has surprised.

trait.name: Keen Hearing And Smell
trait.text: The grep has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.

trait.name: Mimicry
trait.text: The grep can mimic animal sounds and Humanoid voices. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check.

action.name: Claw (Bonus Action)
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) slashing damage.

fields.description:
A grep is an underground scavenger, known for using its keen vision, acute hearing, and silent flight to trick and steal from travelers, hoarding its possessions in well-hidden troves. Arcanists use greps as messengers and scouts, but they excel as retrievers; a grep can be given the name of an important object and sent to find it, returning a short time later with its prize.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 365 (Indie),
		Complete Witch p. 20 (Indie)

fields.name: Mock

trait.name: Shapechanger
trait.text: The mock can use its action to polymorph into an object or back into its true, amorphous form. It can only take the appearance of Tiny objects and prefers the form of gold coins and jewels. Its statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

trait.name: Adhesive (Object Form Only)
trait.text: The mock adheres to anything that touches it. A creature that picks up the mock can't drop it unless it succeeds on a DC 9 Strength check, made with disadvantage. The mock can only adhere to one creature at a time. The mock has advantage on attack rolls against any creature adhered to it.

trait.name: False Appearance (Object Form Only)
trait.text: While the mock remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary object.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) acid damage. If the mock is in object form, the target is subjected to its Adhesive trait.

fields.description:
The diminutive relative of the mimic, the mock is a tiny shapechanger that replicates small, valuable objects to lure in its victims. In the desert, a mock might take the form of a canteen of precious water, and in a dungeon, it may replicate a sizable jewel or a spare gold piece. If an adventurer is caught by surprise, a mock is just as dangerous as its larger relatives, for it can hide in far less conspicuous places.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 366 (Indie),
		Complete Witch p. 22 (Indie)

fields.name: Moon Jelly

trait.name: Bioluminescence
trait.text: The moon jelly sheds dim light in a 10-foot radius.

trait.name: Water Breathing
trait.text: The moon jelly can only breathe underwater.

fields.description:
Though incapable of surviving on land, moon jellies are favored for their bioluminescence by witches that intend to explore deep underwater.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 366 (Indie),
		Complete Witch p. 22 (Indie)

fields.name: Pet Rock
fields.resist: fire, lightning, radiant, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks
fields.conditionImmune: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, unconscious

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: The pet rock is indistinguishable from an ordinary rock with a face drawn on it.

trait.name: Just a Rock
trait.text: The pet rock counts as an object for the purposes of spells and magical effects. Additionally, the rock can't take actions that aren't specified in its statistics, and its speed can't be increased.

fields.description:
Widely considered to be the perfect familiar, requiring no food or water and possessing extremely high natural defenses, a pet rock can be conjured by most spellcasters. Though it doesn't act with any agility (indeed, it doesn't move at all), it can make a formidable weapon when thrown.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 367 (Indie),
		Complete Witch p. 22 (Indie)

fields.name: Rag Doll
fields.immune: poison, psychic, bludgeoning from nonmagical attacks

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: While the rag doll remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal stuffed toy.

trait.name: Mimicry
trait.text: The rag doll can mimic simple sounds it has heard, such as a person whispering, a baby crying, or an animal chittering. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 11 Wisdom (Insight) check.

action.name: Headbutt
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +0 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1 bludgeoning damage.

fields.description:
Crudely constructed but oddly endearing, rag dolls are constructs formed from children's toys, stuffed with soft material and adorned with smiling faces. Besides being generally comforting to have around, spellcasters favor rag dolls as familiars for their soft construction and inconspicuous nature; nobody questions a discarded doll, after all.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 367 (Indie),
		Complete Witch p. 24 (Indie)

fields.name: Tin Soldier

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: While the tin soldier remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal toy.

trait.name: Formation
trait.text: The tin soldier has advantage on attack rolls when it is within 5 feet of another tin soldier.

action.name: Bayonet
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +0 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1 piercing damage.

action.name: Rifle (recharge 6)
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage.

fields.description:
Full of ticking clockwork, sprockets, and other gizmos, tin soldiers are mechanical creations fashioned by arcanists as servants and messengers. With some patience and skill, almost anyone can build a tin soldier, but spellcasters have long devised methods to conjure them wholesale from the Plane of Law's excess energies.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 368 (Indie),
		Complete Witch p. 25 (Indie)

fields.name: Winter Wolf Pup

trait.name: Snow Camouflage
trait.text: The pup has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in snowy terrain.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.

fields.description:
When fully grown, a winter wolf is an apex predator of the snow, a terror of teeth and fur, stalking the tundra in packs. But before they develop their fearsome freezing breath, winter wolf pups are far more amicable (perhaps because they have yet to realize the scope of their own might), and will dutifully follow a master that feeds them well and treats them with respect.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 368 (Indie),
		Complete Witch p. 25 (Indie)

fields.name: Yarn Golem

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: While the golem remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal ball of yarn.

trait.name: Mutable Form
trait.text: Whenever a spell or effect would alter the golem's form, the effect works as normal, except that the new form is always made out of a tangle of yarn.

action.name: Tangle
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: If the target is Medium or smaller, it is grappled (escape DC 12). The yarn golem can only grapple one creature at a time.

fields.description:
The greatest of golems are formed of clay, stone, and iron, but the least of them are constructed of yarn. Balled and sewn into a vaguely humanoid shape, yarn golems are among the first animated objects that arcanists learn to create, practicing with them obsessively until they master the basics and move onto more rigid materials. Yarn golems are friendly and playful, but risk foolishly unraveling themselves if they catch on sharp objects.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 368 (Indie),
		Complete Witch p. 25 (Indie)

fields.name: Abbot Cohort

trait.text: The abbot can use its Healing Hands and Guiding Strike an additional time each when the captain reaches 5th level (2/day each), 11th level (3/day each), and 17th level (4/day each).

trait.name: (10th) Divine Strike
trait.text: The abbot deals an extra 1d8 radiant damage when it hits with an attack roll.

action.name: Mace
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Light Crossbow
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d8) piercing damage.

action.name: Healing Hands (1/Day)
action.text: The abbot or one creature the abbot touches regains 11 (2d8 + 2) hit points.

action.name: (6th) Spellcasting
action.text:
The abbot casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 12):

	• At will: guidance, spare the dying

action.name: (14th) Spellasting
action.text:
The abbot's Spellcasting improves. It can cast the following spells in addition to those in its statistics:

	• 1/day each: death ward, revivify, speak with dead

reaction.name: (18th) Merciful Light (1/Day)
reaction.text: In response to a friendly creature within 30 feet of the abbot taking damage, the abbot causes that creature to regain hit points equal to 2d8 + the abbot's Wisdom modifier.

fields.spells: Guidance, Spare the Dying, Bless, Lesser Restoration, Protection from Evil and Good, Death Ward, Revivify, Speak with Dead
fields.description:
Your cohort is the most steadfast of allies, is loyal to a fault, and will likely be a lifelong ally and friend. But not all cohorts are cut from the same cloth or possess the same skills. Choose from the following nonplayer characters when you enlist a new cohort.
	A devout adherent to the faith, an abbot can work minor divine miracles with the whispering of prayers and the waving of hands.
	While following the command of a captain, the abbot gains additional abilities based on the captain's level:

	2nd. Divine Devotion. The abbot can use its Healing Hands and Guiding Strike an additional time each when the captain reaches 5th level (2/day each), 11th level (3/day each), and 17th level (4/day each).

	6th. Action: Spellcasting. The abbot casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 12):

	• At will: guidance, spare the dying
	• 1/day each: bless, lesser restoration, protection from evil and good

	10th. Divine Strike. The abbot deals an extra 1d8 radiant damage when it hits with an attack roll.

	14th. Action: Spellcasting. The abbot's Spellcasting improves. It can cast the following spells in addition to those in its statistics:

	• 1/day each: death ward, revivify, speak with dead.

	18th. Reaction: Merciful Light (1/Day). In response to a friendly creature within 30 feet of the abbot taking damage, the abbot causes that creature to regain hit points equal to 2d8 + the abbot's Wisdom modifier.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 54 (Indie)

fields.name: Berserker Cohort

trait.name: Unarmored Defense
trait.text: While the berserker is wearing no armor and wielding no shield, its AC includes its Constitution modifier.

trait.name: (2nd) Reckless
trait.text: At the start of its turn, the berserker can gain advantage on all melee weapon attack rolls during that turn, but attack rolls against it have advantage until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: (6th) Relentless (1/Day)
trait.text: If the berserker is reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, it can drop to 1 hit point instead.

trait.name: (14th) Critical Rush
trait.text: Once per turn, when the berserker scores a critical hit, it can move up to its movement speed and make a melee weapon attack with advantage.

trait.name: (18th) Primal Resolve
trait.text: When the berserker has half its hit points or fewer, it has resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

action.name: Greataxe
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d12 + 2) slashing damage.

action.name: Handaxe
action.text: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.

reaction.name: (10th) Retaliation (3/Day)
reaction.text: In response to being hit by a melee attack, the berserker can make one melee weapon attack against the attacker.

fields.description:
Your cohort is the most steadfast of allies, is loyal to a fault, and will likely be a lifelong ally and friend. But not all cohorts are cut from the same cloth or possess the same skills. Choose from the following nonplayer characters when you enlist a new cohort.

Ruthless and fierce, the berserker tears across the battlefield in a wild frenzy, devastating their enemies with boundless rage.

While following the command of a captain, the berserker gains additional abilities based on the captain's level:

	• 2nd. Reckless. At the start of its turn, the berserker can gain advantage on all melee weapon attack rolls during that turn, but attack rolls against it have advantage until the start of its next turn.

	• 6th. Relentless (1/Day). If the berserker is reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, it can drop to 1 hit point instead.

	• 10th. Reaction: Retaliation (3/Day). In response to being hit by a melee attack, the berserker can make one melee weapon attack against the attacker.

	• 14th. Critical Rush. Once per turn, when the berserker scores a critical hit, it can move up to its movement speed and make a melee weapon attack with advantage.

	• 18th. Primal Resolve. When the berserker has half its hit points or fewer, it has resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

Source:	Valda's Spire of Secrets p. 55 (Indie)

trait.text: The champion rerolls a failed saving throw.

action.text: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

action.text: The champion regains 5 hit points. When the captain reaches 6th level, this amount of healing increases to 10, and when the captain reaches 14th level, this amount of healing increases to 20.

A champion is a skilled, tactical fighter, just as comfortable in the saddle during military drills as armored on the field of battle.

While following the command of a captain, the champion gains additional abilities based on the captain's level:

	• 2nd. Bonus Action: Second Wind (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). The champion regains 5 hit points. When the captain reaches 6th level, this amount of healing increases to 10, and when the captain reaches 14th level, this amount of healing increases to 20.

fields.name: Construct Cohort

trait.text: The construct explodes when it drops to 0 hit points. Each creature within 5 feet of it must make a D C 12 Dexterity saving throw, taking 7 (2d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

	With the help of a tinkerer or a mage, you gain the unwavering, mechanical loyalty of a golem, shield guardian, or clockwork construct. Your construct is of a smaller variety than most golems, but can be built and repaired in far less time.

	Constructed Nature. A construct doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

fields.name: Cultist Cohort

trait.name: Dark Devotion

trait.text: A creature that starts its turn within 120 feet of the Amalgamation is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 20. Failure: The target gains a Contamination level. Failure or Success: 14 (4d6) Necrotic damage.

trait.name: Immutable Form
trait.text: The Amalgamation has Immunity to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

trait.name: Malignancy
trait.text: The Amalgamation can't be teleported or travel to another plane against its will.

trait.name: Rejuvenation
trait.text: If the Amalgamation is destroyed in the Mortal World, it reappears 1d10 days later with all of its Hit Points unless its roots in the Space Between Worlds are also destroyed.

trait.name: Ultimate Corruption
trait.text: Necrotic damage dealt by the Amalgamation ignores Resistance and treats Immunity as Resistance instead.

trait.name: Fully Contaminated
trait.text: This creature is immune to Contamination and has Advantage on saving throws against contaminated spells. This creature may cast contaminated spells even though it does not gain Contamination levels.

trait.name: Haze Adaptation
trait.text: This creature may benefit from a Long Rest finished within the Haze. It can see twice as far through the Haze mists and Deep Haze fog as those without this adaption.

trait.name: Haze Dependence
trait.text: This creature gains one level of Exhaustion for every 24 hours it spends outside the Haze. These Exhaustion levels cannot be removed while the creature is outside the Haze.

trait.name: Delerium Healing
trait.text: As a Utilize action, a monster can touch a delerium shard to regain 10 (3d6) Hit Points. Once a monster has used a delerium shard in this way, the shard can't be used in this manner again for 24 hours.

action.name: Epic Actions
action.text: The Amalgamation always takes its turn on initiative count 20. On its turn, the Amalgamation can use its movement and interaction as normal. However, it does not take an action or Bonus Action on its turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, the Amalgamation takes one of the following Epic Actions at the end of each player character's turn:

action.name: Bite
action.text:
Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 10 ft. Hit: 36 (4d12 + 10) Force damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature Grappled by the Amalgamation, the grapple ends and the target is swallowed. While swallowed, the target has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, has Total Cover from effects originating from outside the Amalgamation, and takes 42 (12d6) Necrotic damage and gains a Contamination level at the start of each of the Amalgamation's turns.
	If the Amalgamation takes 50+ damage in a single turn from a creature inside it, it must succeed on a DC 25 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which land in spaces within 10 feet of the Amalgamation and have the Prone condition. If the Amalgamation dies, a swallowed creature no longer has the Restrained condition and can escape the corpse using 15 feet of its movement, exiting with the Prone condition.

action.name: Tentacle
action.text: Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 60 ft. Hit: 28 (4d8 + 10) Force damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 25). While Grappled, the target has the Restrained condition. The Amalgamation has twelve tentacles, each of which can grapple one target.

action.name: Fling
action.text: One Large or smaller object held or creature Grappled by the Amalgamation is thrown up to 60 feet, landing with the Prone condition. If the target strikes a solid surface, it takes 35 (10d6) Force damage. If the target is thrown at another creature, that creature must succeed on a DC 25 Dexterity saving throw or take the same damage and have the Prone condition.

action.name: Mind-breaking Whispers (recharge 5-6)
action.text: Intelligence Saving Throw: DC 25, one creature within 120 feet of the Amalgamation. Failure: The target becomes insane until it finishes a Long Rest. While insane, the target can't take actions, understand other creatures, read, or speak anything but gibberish. A Greater Restoration or Heal spell ends the effect early. Failure or Success: 70 (20d6) Psychic damage.

action.name: Forced Mutation (1/Round)
action.text: Each creature within 120 feet of the Amalgamation with one or more Contamination levels takes 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage and gains a randomly determined mutation.

action.name: Piper At the Gate (1/Round)
action.text: A Pyknic Maunder appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of the Amalgamation, acting after the Amalgamation on Initiative count 20 and under the Amalgamation's direct control. The Amalgamation can have up to ten Pyknic Maunders under its control at a time.

action.name: Epic Resistance
action.text: The Amalgamation chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting them and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on it. The Amalgamation can use this Epic Action even if it would otherwise be unable to take actions, its actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters its game statistics.

fields.description:
Before the throne is a gibbering amalgamation of fleshy tumors, rotting bones, and rancid layers of bloated fat suspended between the ceiling and floor by stalky strands of gnarled tissue. A palpable aura of contamination emanates from the beast. The mass is covered in bursting sores and shuddering mucus nodules that weep bile and delerium sludge. The creature mutters in alien tongues from six yawning mouths, piping and sputtering in discordant musical tones, and lazily shifting eyes of massive size open and close throughout its bulk. Thick trunk-like tentacles reach out from its hideous stinking form to squirm and writhe around the chamber. Several appendages are wrapped around pulsing human organs: lungs, liver, kidney, a heart, a brain, and dangling amongst them is the jeweled Crown of Westemär.

Study the Foe:
Characters who have one or more mutations, or who are afflicted with any form of madness gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks when they Study the Amalgamation, learning the following based on the result:

(20+) Multidimensional. You recognize its Immunities, and its Rejuvenation, Malignancy, and Immutable Form traits.
(25+) Insatiable Hunger. You know of the creature's Bite attack, as well as its Mind-Breaking Whispers ability.
(30+) Beyond Comprehension. You are aware of its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
The Amalgamation is a formidable foe capable of grappling multiple targets and eating them or throwing them around the battlefield. It constantly summons Pyknic Maunders as additional support while it uses Mind-Breaking Whispers to shatter the minds of its greatest threats.
	The Amalgamation does not fear any mortal creature, believing itself indestructible to mortal means. It does not flee or cower.

Harvestable Components (Legendary):
Animus: Aberration.
Fluid: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor, Goopy Ooze, Acidic Bile.
Organs: Eyes, Heart, Flesh, Guts.
Natural Weapons: Tentacles, Teeth.
Hair: Hair.
Hide: Skin.
Dust: Aberrant Dust.
Trophy: The Crown of Westemär.

Source:	Pluto Jackson's Monsters of Drakkenheim p. 24 (Third Party)

fields.resist: spell damage, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks

A creature that ends its turn in the mucus is covered in goop and subjected to the following effect. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 17. Failure: 20 (8d4) Acid damage, and the target has the Slowed condition. Each time the creature ends its turn with the Slowed condition, it gains a Contamination level. A creature within 5 feet can take an action to clean away the goop, ending the Slowed condition.

action.name: Slobber
action.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 20 (8d4) Acid damage.

action.name: Creep
action.text: The anomollusk moves up to its Speed, and can enter the spaces of Large or smaller creatures as it does. Each creature whose space it enters is subjected once to the following effect. Strength Saving Throw: DC 17. Success: The target is pushed 5 feet away from the anomollusk into a space of its choice. If the target chooses not to move, it suffers the effects of a failure. Failure: The target has the Prone condition and is subjected to Snail Trail.

reaction.name: Shell Reflection
reaction.text: Trigger: The anomollusk takes damage from a spell or magical attack. Response: The attacker takes Radiant damage equal to the triggering damage and causes an Arcane Anomaly.

fields.description:
A colossal snail as wide as a city street with a shell the size of a small house glides slowly into view. Its shell has a kaleidoscopic fractal shimmer, projecting hues of unknown colors that swirl in incomprehensible patterns. As it moves, its shell seems to refract light in ways that seem nonsensical or wrong. You must strain your eyes to look at it wriggle towards you. Its bulbous head ends in two long antennae each holding a small octarine eye. Slimy mucus drips off its flesh, leaving sizzling trails and corroding anything it touches.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Animal Handling or Survival gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks to Study an Anomollusk, learning the following based on the result:
(10+) Powerfully Protected. You learn its Resistances as well as its Shell Reflection Reaction.
(15+) Dangerous Slime. You are aware of its Snail Trail and Creep abilities.
(20+) Slow and Simple Minded. You recognize its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
Drawn to magic, Anomollusk's view spellcasters and those equipped with magic items as delicious morsels. It attacks by first using its Creep action before it tries to Slobber on them. If threatened, it tries to cover the enemy and its territory in acidic slime. If reduced to less than half Hit Points, it attempts to flee.

Harvestable Components (Rare):
Animus: Monstrosity.
Fluid: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor, Goopy Ooze, Acidic Bile, Mucus.
Organs: Eyes, Guts, Glands.
Hide: Shell, Skin.

Source:	Pluto Jackson's Monsters of Drakkenheim p. 26 (Third Party)

action.text: The arcane wraith makes three Comet Shard attacks.

action.name: Comet Shard
action.text: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 21 (4d8 + 3) Force damage, and the target is pushed 10 feet away from the arcane wraith.

action.name: Nightmare Pattern (recharge 5-6)
action.text: Intelligence Saving Throw: DC 14, each creature in a 30-foot Cube centered on a point the arcane wraith can see. Failure: The target has the Blinded condition (save ends). While Blinded, the target has the Immobilized condition. The effect ends for the target if it takes damage or another creature takes an action to shake it out of its nightmare. When the effect ends, the target takes 14 (4d6) Psychic damage.

action.name: Spellcasting
action.text:
The arcane wraith casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14):

	• At Will: Mage Hand (the hand is Invisible), Minor Illusion

fields.spells: Mage Hand, Minor Illusion
fields.description:
Tattered purple robes hang off the ethereal skeleton drifting silently through the air. Its rune-inscribed skull menacingly chants arcane words as points of octarine light flare from the dark holes of its eyes. Ghostly tendrils flicker and five Academy rings jangle as it raises a skeletal hand, enacting the arcane gestures of its first spell.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Arcana gain Advantage on Intelligence (Religion) checks to Study an Arcane Wraith, learning the following based on the result:
(5+) Contaminated Undead. You know the Arcane Wraith's Immunities and Resistances.
(10+) Spellcaster's Spirit. You are aware of its Comet Shards and Nightmare Pattern actions.
(15+) Unstable Intellect. You recognize the monster's strongest ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
Arcane Wraiths take advantage of their Incorporeal Movement, gliding through walls and small openings, before blasting targets with Comet Shards from above. They use Nightmare Pattern to control foes and focus attacks on those unaffected by the illusion. Occasionally, they collaborate with other undead, such as Haze Husks and Haze Wights, commanding them like apprentices or minions.

Harvestable Components (Rare):
Animus: Undead.
Fluid: Contaminated Ichor, Ectoplasm.
Dust: Undead Dust.
Items: Arcane Wraiths often have 1d3 uncommon potions or spell scrolls collected nearby and may occasionally have a spellbook with 2d6 wizard spells of 3rd level and lower scribbled inside.

Source:	Pluto Jackson's Monsters of Drakkenheim p. 27 (Third Party)

Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Piercing damage, or 26 (4d10 + 4) Piercing damage if the beetle knight moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit. If the target is Medium or smaller, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14). While Grappled, the target has the Restrained condition and the beetle knight can't use its Pincer Horn against another target.

reaction.name: Carapace Parry
reaction.text: Trigger: A creature the beetle knight can see hits it with an attack. Response: The beetle knight adds 2 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

fields.description:
Two insectoid legs hold up the beetle-like creature, rhythmically clacking as it skitters about. Two clawed arms scrabble beneath blade-like limbs as gnashing mandibles chitter under its beady eyes. A massive pincer-like horn protrudes from its helmet-shaped head and a tough blueish-silver shell protects delicate wings hidden beneath.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Animal Handling or Nature gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks to study a Beetle Knight, revealing the following based on the result:
(5+) Alien and Unflinching. You identify its condition Immunities.
(10+) Watch Out for that Horn! You recognize its Fling Bonus Action, and Pincer Horn action.
(15+) Slow and Unintelligent. You know its strongest and weakest saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
The Beetle Knight is surprisingly agile, rarely standing still in battle. They charge during the first round, flinging enemies aside or attempting to grapple. If possible, they back up to charge again but will otherwise defend with their arm blades. They attempt to flee losing battles where their Hit Points fall below half their maximum.

fields.description:
A shrill screech pierces the air as a large, misshapen bat swoops overhead. Its outstretched wings resemble elongated human arms, with flesh pulled taut to its deformed body. Rows of hooked fangs fill its maw below bulging, red eyes and a snivelling snout.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Nature or Survival gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks to Study a Belfray, learning the following based on their result:
(5+) Accustomed to the Dark. You understand the Belfray's damage Resistances and Immunities.
(10+) Flying Blood-Drinker. You recognize its Flyby and Keen Hearing features, and Enfeebling Bite attack.
(15+) Weak Mind. You know the Belfray's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
The Belfray attempts to strike with a Sonic Blast from the shadows before engaging. Once a target is weakened, it swoops in with its claws. When damaged, Belfrays Bite, feeding on the blood of their victims to regain strength. It uses movement to stay away from threats, diving to attack before flying to a safe distance. If reduced below half of its maximum Hit Points, it attempts to fly away.

fields.description:
The ground shudders beneath the approach of a monstrosity: a pale, green-white, bipedal reptile. A huge mouth dominates its skull-like face, as acidic saliva drips between rows of razor-sharp teeth. Spines run down its back and tail, and its great body is supported by two trunk-like legs, though its feeble forearms appear nearly useless. It roars a sound like rent metal as it charges forward to devour you.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Nature or Survival gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks to Study Big Linda, revealing the following based on their result:
(10+) Hard to Kill. You know Big Linda's damage Immunities as well as its Rejuvenation and Regeneration traits.
(15+) Acidic Mucus! You're aware of her Acid Spew attack.
(20+) Big, Clumsy, and Dumb. You recognize Big Linda's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
Big Linda sends Acid Spew against groups of opponents. She then tries to optimize her Bite and Tail attacks by placing herself within her enemies. She is hesitant to leave the Deep Haze but is also not smart enough to resist chasing those who are antagonizing her. She rarely flees unless severely wounded, wherein she will seek the safety of the Deep Haze to recover.

Bigger Linda can use this Epic Action even if she would otherwise be unable to take actions, her actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters her game statistics.

fields.description:
Thundering through the streets of Drakkenheim with a crash, the infamous pet of the Queen of Thieves has mutated and enlarged to unfathomable proportions. The Haze swirls around it, and octarine energy pulses in its sunken eye sockets. The broken hafts of weapons and old arrows are embedded into its scales, stuck deeply between its regenerated flesh. Its spined back is illuminated by webs of glowing octarine veins; its wide snout is filled with jagged teeth. As it opens its maw wide, the building contaminated energy at the back of its throat begins to glow.

Source:	Pluto Jackson's Monsters of Drakkenheim p. 31 (Third Party)

action.text: The bloated hive causes its Insect Swarm to fly in the face of a creature within 5 feet of it. The target can't take Reactions until the end of the bloated hive's turn.

fields.description:
Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Nature or Survival gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks to Study a Bloated Hive, recognizing the following based on their result:
(5+) Sightless Awareness. You know the creature's Immunities and senses.
(10+) Endless insects! You are aware of the creature's Spawn Swarm action and Disrupt the Hive trait.
(15+) Frail. You recognize the Bloated Hive's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
The Bloated Hive is usually a solitary creature that spends its time cowering in dark corners living out its cursed life as nothing more than a conduit for its colony. In combat, they focus entirely on keeping their distance from threats and spawning swarms of insects to defend themselves. If cornered, the Bloated Hive uses its Claws and Distracting Swarm before moving back into the shadows and attempting to escape and find a new nest.
	Larger packs of Bloated Hives are much braver and more violent, and actively hunt and pursue targets until their numbers are less than their prey. Places where large colonies gather are dangerous. The Bloated Hives work in unison to protect their nests. Only if they become outnumbered do they flee.

fields.description:
This creature, which appears to be a dead horse flopped on its back, convulses and its stomach suddenly splits open, exposing its intestines and organs. Long, spindly, arachnid-like legs violently sprout from its torso as its stomach opens into a maw filled with sharp jagged teeth formed from the splayed rib cage of the beast. The horse legs limply hang in the air, as the creature skitters towards you with intense speed, intestines flapping around its maw like a sickly tongue. The head of the horse dangles lifelessly, but its mouth still gnashes and salivates acidic bile.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Nature or Survival gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks to Study a Bojack, learn the following based on their result:
(10+) Parasitic Mutation. You recognize the BoJack's Immunities and senses.
(15+) Acidic Ambusher. You're aware of the creature's Corrosive Mucus and Impaling Limbs attacks.
(20+) Fast and Cunning. You know the Bojack's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
The Bojack is an ambush skirmisher. It waits for the opportune moment to strike, attempting to surprise as many targets as possible. After it surprises its prey, it attacks with its Impaling Limbs or Corrosive Mucus and uses its Predatory Cunning to move out of melee range.
	The Bojack can climb walls and will try and skitter up buildings or behind walls, springing back out to attack before escaping again. If brought below 20 Hit Points, the BoJack attempts to Dash away and Hide.

fields.name: Cacophonous Chimera (Epic)

trait.name: Epic Foe
trait.text:
This is an epic foe, following the rules as described in Pluto Jackson's Monsters of Drakkenheim.

To calculate its Max HP use the following calculation: 54 (4d12 + 28) plus 54 (4d12 + 28) per player character.

trait.name: Cacophonous Chorus
trait.text: The cacophonous chimera creates a 30-foot Emanation of noise. A creature that starts its turn in the Emanation that can hear it takes 10 (3d6) Thunder damage.

trait.name: Keen Sight and Smell
trait.text: The cacophonous chimera has Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Fully Contaminated
trait.text: This creature is immune to Contamination and has Advantage on saving throws against contaminated spells. This creature may cast contaminated spells even though it does not gain Contamination levels.

trait.text: As a Utilize action, a monster can touch a delerium shard to regain 10 (3d6) Hit Points. Once a monster has used a delerium shard in this way, the shard can't be used in this manner again for 24 hours.

action.name: Epic Actions
action.text: The cacophonous chimera always takes its turn on Initiative count 20. On its turn, the cacophonous chimera can use its movement and interaction as normal. However, it does not take an action or Bonus Action on its turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, the cacophonous chimera takes one of the following Epic Actions at the end of each player character's turn:

action.name: Claws and Talons
action.text: Melee Attack Roll: +11, reach 10 ft. Hit: 11 (1d10 + 6) Slashing damage, and if the target is Large or smaller, it has the Prone condition.

action.name: Contaminated Bite (1/Round)
action.text: Melee Attack Roll: +11, reach 10 ft. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) Piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 17. Failure: The target gains a Contamination level.

action.name: Lamprey Tail
action.text: Melee Attack Roll: +11, reach 30 ft. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) Piercing damage, and the target has the Bleeding condition (2d4).

action.name: Aerial Maneuver (1/Round)
action.text: The cacophonous chimera flies up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

action.name: Cacophony (1/Round)
action.text:
The cacophonous chimera's three heads sing a discordant song. The effect of the song varies based on which of the chimera's head is taking the lead. Each time the cacophonous chimera uses this Epic Action, it can't use the same effect it chose last round.

	Bewildering Chitter (Ratling). Intelligence Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature in a 300-foot Emanation originating from the chimera that can hear it. Failure: 10 (3d6) Psychic damage, and the target has the Bewildered condition (save ends).

	Chilling Howl (Garmyr). Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature in a 300-foot Emanation originating from the cacophonous chimera that can hear it. Failure: 10 (3d6) Cold damage, and the target has the Immobilized condition (save ends).

	Staggering Screech (Harpy). Charisma Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature in a 300-foot Emanation originating from the cacophonous chimera that can hear it. Failure: 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage, and the target has the Staggered condition (save ends).

action.name: Wing Blast
action.text: Strength Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature within 15 feet of the cacophonous chimera. Failure: 13 (2d6 + 6) Thunder damage, and the target is pushed 10 feet away from the chimera. Success: Half damage only.

action.name: Epic Resistance
action.text: The cacophonous chimera chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting them and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on it. The cacophonous chimera can use this Epic Action even if it would otherwise be unable to take actions, its actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters its game statistics.

reaction.name: Crescendo of Chaos (1/Day)
reaction.text:
Trigger: The cacophonous chimera becomes Bloodied. It can take this Reaction even if it has the Incapacitated condition or is otherwise unable to take Reactions. Response: All conditions and spells on the cacophonous chimera immediately end unless it chooses to be affected by them, and it can move up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks and ignoring Difficult Terrain.
	It then unleashes a blast of thunderous power. Creatures within 300 feet of it who can hear it are subjected to the following effect. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 17. Failure: 17 (5d6) Thunder damage plus 17 (5d6) Psychic damage, and the target has the Prone condition and can't stand until the end of its next turn.

fields.description:
The Cacophonous Chimera's three heads include a chittering rat, a screeching harpy, and a howling garmyr, which together perform a madness-inducing chorus as they slaughter their prey. Its forelimbs are clawed rat-like paws, its rear legs are avian talons, and the beast's colossal furry body is borne upon massive wings of blood-red feathers with a slithering lamprey eel for a tail.

Roleplaying Traits:
The following traits can be used to inspire roleplaying the Cacophonous Chimera:
	• Personality Trait: "Just ONCE can we chat with someone a little before we eat them? RARGH! STOP TALKING! RIP AND TEAR! NO! NO! NO! Our stomach is FOUR TIMES bigger than it used to be! I'm STARVING!"
	• Bond: "We're fused together. Although each of us wants to be separated, in truth we're afraid of what would happen if we were ever torn apart."
	• Ideal: "I make such wonderful music! Each howl, shriek, and chitter resonates to form a deadly orchestra. I can't stand silence!"
	• Flaw: "We're constantly arguing. Our internal strife often distracts us from opportunities or leads us into traps, as we can't agree even on the simplest decisions."

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Nature or Survival gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks when they Study a Cacophonous Chimera, learning the following based on their result:
(15+) Freakish Fusion. You're aware of the chimera's Epic Resistance Epic Action.
(20+) Fighting for Control. You recognize the chimera's Cacophony Epic Action, noting that if the creature could be silenced, it would be far less formidable.
(25+) Powerful but Distracted. You understand its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
Desperate to eat and consume, the Cacophonous Chimera viciously attacks prey on sight despite the desires of its harpy head to engage in a little conversation first. The Cacophonous Chimera is not a very subtle hunter. Its prey can hear it coming by the sound of its droning cacophony from at least a city block away, which may give them opportunity to prepare, hide, or flee.
	The range of its Cacophony can affect creatures before they can see the chimera itself. By the time the chimera arrives, its prey may be shaken and immobilized by the sound. Depending on how ravenous and furious it is, the chimera closes with its prey and tears them apart using its Claws, Bite, and Tail.
	Against a target that shows resilience to its cacophony or who retaliates with formidable attacks of their own, the chimera keeps a middle distance, trying to keep out of melee range while leaving its foes in its Cacophonous Chorus aura. However, its ravenous Garmyr head and Ratling head can often get in the way of the better judgment here, prompting the chimera to engage in melee even when it would not be advantageous. Furthermore, the three creatures are generally too busy arguing or overconfident to think twice about the actual danger and stakes they might be facing, and so may need to be grievously wounded before fleeing is an option.

fields.description:
Scampering up the wall is a creature the size of a hound. It resembles a mostly hairless squirrel save for its bushy tail and patchy tufts of mottled fur. Its eyes are glassy and milk white, and its mouth seems almost human, sporting huge, pearly white teeth that grin maniacally. It frantically clambers upward, while chittering a maddening chorus with its clacking teeth.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Animal Handling gain Advantage on Intelligence (Nature) checks to Study a Chitter, learning the following based on their result:
(5+) Wall Crawling. You are aware of its climb speed, its Running Leap trait, and its Slow Fall feature.
(10+) Madding Noise. You know of its Chitter attack action.
(15+) Simple Minded. You recognize its mental ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
Chitters often attack in a small group. Usually two to three that form a family will stick together. The mutated squirrels have been known to be quite territorial and hostile, even to other Chitter families who try to infringe on their territory.
	Chitters are excellent climbers, capable of falling a great distance without fear of hurting themselves. It is not uncommon for Chitters to be found in tall buildings, or up on the top floor of ruined houses, or hard-to-reach rooftops or attics. Chitters charge their enemies and leap at them, attempting to disable them with their chittering, and relying on their Claws and Bite. Chitters protect their homes with determined ferocity, but if reduced to less than a third of their Hit Points, they leap and clamber away.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The crater wurm makes a Bite attack, then makes Bite attacks against each creature adjacent to the first target.

action.name: Bite
action.text:
Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 10 ft. Hit: 35 (4d12 + 9) Piercing damage, and if it is Large or smaller, the target is subjected to the following effect. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 22. Failure: The target is swallowed by the wurm. The target has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, has Total Cover against effects originating from outside the wurm, and takes 36 (8d8) Necrotic damage at the start of each of the wurm's turns. A creature that takes this Necrotic damage must also succeed on a DC 19 Constitution saving throw or gain one Contamination level.
	If the wurm takes 30+ damage on a single turn from a creature inside it, it must succeed on a DC 21 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which land in spaces within 10 feet of the wurm with the Prone condition. If the wurm dies, a swallowed creature no longer has the Restrained condition and can escape from the corpse using 20 feet of movement, exiting with the Prone condition.

action.name: Breach
action.text: The wurm moves up to its Speed, entering the spaces of Large or smaller creatures. Each creature whose space it enters is subjected once to the following effect. At the end of its movement, the wurm can make one Bite attack against a Prone creature as a Bonus Action. Strength Saving Throw: DC 22. Success: The target is pushed 5 feet away from the wurm into a space of its choice. If the target chooses not to move, it suffers the effects of a failure. Failure: 35 (10d6) Bludgeoning damage, and the target is pushed 10 feet away from the wurm and has the Prone condition.

fields.description:
The earth trembles, vibrating pebbles and dust. A deep rumble wells from below. Suddenly, stone cracks, extruding a titanic wurm. It rears its massive head, opening a petal-like mouth filled with long jagged crystalline teeth all pointed into its throat. Its body is covered in muddy purple plates with octarine spines jutting from between. Its hot breath sends octarine slime flying as it dives toward you.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Nature or Survival gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks when they Study a Crater Wurm, learning the following based on their result:
(15+) Subterranean Threat. You know it has Tremorsense and that it creates tunnels when digging through rock.
(20+) Earth Shaker. You're aware of the Crater Wurms' Breach and Bite attacks.
(25+) Blunderous Brute. You recognize the Crater Wurms' strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
Crater Wurms disregard other creatures, viewing them as only morsels to consume. All are as the dust of the earth to it—simply food. These wurms understand that creatures they devour often try to flee. Their favored tactic is to remain buried until their Tremorsense detects movement. They then surface with its Breach action, making Bite attacks, swallowing nearby Prone creatures. They dive beneath the ground once at least one creature is swallowed, or if reduced to half its Hit Point maximum.

Hide: Plates.

Failure: The target is infected with a disease called Dark Decay. Instead of acting normally on its turn, the target must move toward the closest creature that isn't infected with Dark Decay and make one melee attack against it. If the attack hits, the target of that attack must also make a saving throw against Dark Decay. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save. Subsequent Failures: The target gains one Contamination level. Third Success: The disease ends.
	An infected creature that dies or undergoes a Monstrous Transformation becomes a Dark Growth Shambler. A Lesser Restoration spell or similar magic that removes diseases ends Dark Decay, as does any magic that removes Contamination levels.

fields.description:
The remains of a corpse is splayed across a ruined wall. A chaotic mass of jet-black brambles and vines pours from its torso, clinging to the nearby stonework. Branches have burst from its form, and its neck erupts into another mass of plant matter. The skull is severed from the body with its jaw unhinged and hanging in a horrible expression, stuck in place by the writhing vines. Throughout this Dark Growth, flowers bloom in iridescent neon hues and the smell of sweet pollen and decaying flesh fills the air. You hear gentle whispers from a distant voice, distinctly familiar and beckoning.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Survival gain Advantage on Intelligence (Nature) checks to Study a Dark Growth, learning the following based on their result:
(5+) Contaminated and Thriving. You are aware of the Dark Growth's Resistances and Immunities.
(10+) Deadly Spores. You recognize the creature's Infection Spores action.
(15+) Kill it with fire! You know the creature's Vulnerability to Fire, and its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
A Dark Growth is a simple-minded plant. It uses Mimicry to lure passing creatures towards it, often mimicking the sounds of children or people in need. It entangles and infests any target near it, infecting it with its spores. The creature is a stationary plant and does not flee.

Organs: Flowers.
Bones: Stems.
Natural Weapons: Spores, Needles.
Hair: Leaves.
Dust: Plant Dust.

Source:	Pluto Jackson's Monsters of Drakkenheim p. 40 (Third Party)

fields.description:
Staggering from the shadows is a gaunt humanoid with pale flesh and a hunched form. Vines and branches protrude from its gaping mouth and push through its flesh throughout its body. Flowers emerge from these growths, blooming in iridescent neon hues. A smell of sweet sugar and decaying flesh fills the air, and whispers begin to emerge from it even though the creature's mouth doesn't move.

Source:	Pluto Jackson's Monsters of Drakkenheim p. 41 (Third Party)

At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second Failure: The target has the Immobilized condition. Third Failure: The target has the Paralyzed condition. Success: Half damage only.

fields.description:
Scuttling atop dozens of spindly legs, this grotesque creature resembles a mutated centipede grown to horrific proportions. A segmented body nearly thirty feet long undulates atop unnaturally bending limbs resembling emaciated human fingers. Elongated yellow fingernails crackle and scrape the ground menacingly as it moves. Dominating its fat, round head is a single, massive human-like eye that swivels frenetically with a disturbing, unyielding intensity. Its antenna sprouts above like an eyebrow, while tightly closed mandibles resemble bags under the eye. Its foremost finger-legs end in pincer-like talons thrumming with electricity.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Nature gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks to Study a Digipede, learning the following based on their result:
(10+) Charged Form. You recognize the creature's Resistance to Lightning damage and that it has Tremorsense thanks to its large antenna.
(15+) Sharp and Shocking. You are aware of the Digipede's Talons and Eye Beam actions.
(20+) Insectile Predator. You learn the creature's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
Despite its size, a Digipede will try to hide along rooftops, dark corners, narrow alleys, and any crevice which can accommodate it. It launches its Eye Beam from hiding to hinder its prey's escape, then rips into them with its Talons and Bite. The electric shocks from its attacks disrupt the ability of its prey to effectively fight back.

action.text: Melee Attack Roll: +11, reach 15 ft. Hit: 25 (4d8 + 7) Bludgeoning damage, and the target is pushed 20 feet away from the sewer gator and has the Prone condition.

fields.description:
Surfacing from the rancid sewer waters is a terrible alligator nearly fifty feet long. A jagged ridge of delerium runs along its back, ending in a fell crown atop its head as pallid skin frames its octarine glowing eyes. A thick, purple tentacle-like tongue undulates out of its tooth-filled maw. Strong and sturdy legs support its scarred body, attesting to countless battles in the ruins.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Animal Handling gain Advantage on Intelligence (Nature) checks to study a Drakkenheim Sewer Gator, learning the following based on their result:
(5+) Fearless Aquatic Predator! You learn the Drakkenheim Sewer Gator's condition Immunities and Swim speed.
(10+) Watch out for its bite! You are aware of the creature's Crushing Bite and Death Roll actions.
(15+) Get it out of the water! You know of the creature's Contaminated Regeneration trait.

Combat Tactics:
The Drakkenheim Sewer Gator is primarily aquatic, haunting the sewer system or the Drann River. These monstrosities lunge from the waters to grab prey, dragging it beneath the surface. Once a target is in its jaws, the gator Death Rolls until its victim stops moving. It is a cunning hunter, knowing how to disappear below murky waters, but it can be provoked to chase its prey. Out of the water it is vulnerable and flees if reduced below half its Hit Points.

fields.description:
A translucent bulbous mass floats through the air gently, throbbing neon colors radiating across its skin like a cosmic nebula or an eldritch borealis. A mass of thin strands dangle down from of the creature, pulsating with bioluminescent light. The tendrils move and glide about, gently groping and grabbing at objects as it passes by. The whole creature glows, illuminating the darkened city streets around it. A distant chorus of ethereal hums and tones fill the air.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Nature gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks to Study an Effulgent Cnidarian, learning the following based on their result:
(5+) Aberrant Resistance. You recognize the monster's Immunities and Resistances.
(10+) Hypnotic Color Change. You learn of the monster's Hallucinogenic Bioluminescence trait.
(15+) Weak but Aware. You are aware of the monster's Strength and Dexterity ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
The Effulgent Cnidarians are not predatorial — they only want to bask in the glow of delerium crystals, feeding slowly on the arcane energies they emit. They are, however, protective of their food sources. If creatures venture into an area of heavy delerium crystallization, they are sure to find a few Cnidarians bobbing about. The Cnidarian prefers to use its Hallucinogenic Bioluminescence to dissuade threats from engaging it, instead hoping to cause its enemies to kill one another. The Cnidarians feed on creatures under its hypnosis, absorbing their essence through its tendrils. If attacked, it uses its Reflexive Flash and attempts to move away from its threats, often floating straight up as quickly as it can and out of the reach of danger. Cnidarians do not stay around to fight. If all targets have avoided its charm, and are actively attacking it, it abandons its  food source to seek other safer areas.

fields.description:
A mound of iridescently streaked black muck lumbers through the ruins, splashing with each ponderous step. The sludge reshapes into a towering, almost human-like form, with slimy arms and thick unsteady legs. A head bubbles atop its viscous body revealing a slime drooling maw and two hollows for eyes. Yet, it carries a strangely mirthful expression, as if finding joy in its grotesque existence. The mound emits a gravelly roar, full of sinister glee, and barrels towards you, undeterred by the debris in its way.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Nature gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks when they Study an Animated Delerium Sludge, learning the following based on their result:
(10+) Malleable and Resilient. You learn of the creature's Immunities.
(15+) Contamination by Contact. You are aware of its Contaminated Touch and Engulf actions.
(20+) Easy to Outwit. You know the elemental's mental ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
Animated Delerium Sludge often lies dormant in bodies of water before attempting to Engulf an unsuspecting creature. If reduced to less than 20 Hit Points, it attempts to slip back into the nearby sludge and Hide, hoping to be left alone.

fields.description:
An elemental alight with purple-green flames illuminates the desolate streets ahead. Composed of cascading octarine fire, the elemental moves like wildfire spreading uncontrollably. Within the dancing flames is a scornful expression of rage. It crackles and blazes, the heat from its body distorting the air around it. The pungent smell of burning ozone and sulfur saturates the area, and flecks of cinder and ash whirl about, shedding from the creature as it glides menacingly toward you.

Study the Foe:
Characters proficient in Nature gain Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks when they Study an Entropic Flame, learning the following based on their result:
(10+) Supernaturally Resilient. You are aware of the creature's Immunities.
(15+) Inextinguishable Fires. You learn of the elemental's Dancing Flame action and Flickerjump Bonus Action, as well as its Enduring Flame trait.
(20+) Swift and Senseless. You know the creature's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

Combat Tactics:
An Entropic Flame is a haughty combatant driven by a burning desire to set the world on fire. It teleports from place to place using its Flickerjump, setting alight creatures and objects using its Dancing Flames. If possible, it tries to remain close to Burning targets to keep them on fire within its Enduring Flame aura. Within the smoking ruins of Drakkenheim, Entropic Flames love to set buildings, furniture, and other objects on fire. They quickly turn the battlefield into a roiling inferno, one which cannot be extinguished easily thanks to their presence.

The Haze enveloping you begins to churn and swirl, gradually coalescing into a dense mass of octarine fog. A ghostly visage emerges as a nebulous form takes shape, its features twisted in an eerie semblance of anguish. Flashes of contaminated energy crackle and spark inside the cloud, casting fleeting, sinister lights which mimic the movements of a tortured face. This roiling fog floats through the ruins, drifting like a specter haunted by its own turbulent essence.

(10+) Mundane Immunity. You are aware of the elemental's Immunities.
(15+) Animate Haze. You know of the creature's Fog Form and Deep Haze traits.
(20+) Fast but Dim-Witted. You understand its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

When it encounters an uncontaminated creature, the Living Deep Haze rapidly moves into its space thanks to its Fog Form trait. It then tries to remain there as much as possible so the creature is exposed to its Deep Haze trait. The Living Deep Haze wants to transform its targets into monsters, so it uses its Slam attacks to knock them Unconscious so they can awaken to a new existence as mutant horrors.
